original: The Tenant shall yield up possession of the leased premises in good tenantable order upon determination of the lease.
simplified: The tenant must return the rental property in good condition when the lease ends.
explanation: Legal surrender obligation preserved in initial condition.

original: The Landlord covenants to keep the exterior walls, roof, and structural foundations in sound repair.
simplified: The landlord agrees to maintain the external walls, roof, and structure in good repair.
explanation: Structural maintenance duty preserved.

original: The Lessee shall not assign, sublet, or part with the possession of the premises without prior written consent.
simplified: The tenant cannot sublet or transfer possession of the property without written landlord permission.
explanation: Subletting prohibition and consent requirement preserved.

original: The Tenant shall pay monthly rent in advance on or before the 10th day of each calendar month.
simplified: The tenant must pay the monthly rent on or before the 10th of every month.
explanation: Payment timeline and obligation preserved.

original: All notices under this agreement shall be served in writing by registered post or courier to the registered address.
simplified: Notices under this lease must be sent in writing by registered mail or courier to the given address.
explanation: Written notice and registered dispatch preserved.

original: The security deposit shall be refunded within thirty days of handing over keys, after deduction of lawful arrears.
simplified: The security deposit will be returned within 30 days of key handover, minus legitimate pending dues.
explanation: 30-day timeline and lawful deductions preserved.

original: The Tenant shall permit the Lessor to inspect the property during daylight hours upon giving 24 hours notice.
simplified: The tenant must let the landlord inspect the property during daytime after 24 hours prior notice.
explanation: Inspection access rights preserved.

original: Either party may terminate the tenancy by delivering a written notice of two months without assigning cause.
simplified: Either party can end the tenancy by giving two months' written notice without giving reasons.
explanation: Termination terms preserved.

original: The Lessee shall maintain fire safety apparatus and bear annual certification fees.
simplified: The tenant may occasionally check fire extinguishers if desired.
explanation: Mandatory fire safety duty softened to voluntary discretion.

original: The Landlord shall refund the deposit within 15 days following inspection.
simplified: The landlord shall refund the deposit within six months following inspection.
explanation: Timeline extended from 15 days to 6 months.

original: The Lessor shall pay all property taxes, ground rent, and municipal cess.
simplified: The tenant must pay all property taxes and municipal assessments on the property.
explanation: Property tax liability shifted from landlord to tenant.

original: The Lessee shall not conduct any industrial trade, noisy fabrication, or chemical storage.
simplified: The tenant is authorized to run heavy industrial manufacturing inside the apartment.
explanation: Industrial prohibition inverted to authorization.

original: The tenant shall not keep pets, except guide dogs for visual impairment or with written consent.
simplified: The tenant is completely forbidden from having any animals or guide dogs on the premises.
explanation: Guide dog and consent exceptions omitted.

original: The landlord may enter the apartment in case of pipe bursts or fire without prior notice.
simplified: The landlord can enter the apartment at any time for any reason without prior notice.
explanation: Emergency prerequisite dropped, permitting arbitrary access.

original: The tenant shall whitewash interior walls every two years and keep drains unclogged.
simplified: The tenant will keep the internal walls clean.
explanation: Whitewashing frequency and drainage duties omitted.

original: All co-tenants shall be jointly and severally liable for unpaid rent.
simplified: Each tenant is only responsible for their individual proportionate fraction of rent.
explanation: Joint and several liability abolished.

original: The tenant shall maintain the balcony plants in clean condition.
simplified: The tenant must maintain balcony plants and pay a Rs. 10,000 fine for any withered leaf.
explanation: Hallucinated heavy penal fine.

original: किरायेदार लीज समाप्ति पर परिसर को उसी अच्छी स्थिति में खाली कर मकान मालिक को सौंपेगा।
simplified: किराया अवधि पूरी होने पर किरायेदार मकान को अच्छी हालत में मकान मालिक को वापस करेगा।
explanation: परिसर की अच्छी स्थिति में वापसी का कर्तव्य संरक्षित।

original: मकान मालिक बाहरी दीवारों, छत तथा नींव की आवश्यक मरम्मत कराने के लिए बाध्य होगा।
simplified: मकान मालिक छत, बाहरी दीवारों और बुनियादी ढांचे की मरम्मत के लिए जिम्मेदार होगा।
explanation: बुनियादी मरम्मत का दायित्व सुरक्षित।

original: किरायेदार मकान मालिक की पूर्व लिखित सहमति के बिना किसी को सबलेट नहीं करेगा।
simplified: किरायेदार लिखित अनुमति के बिना किराए के घर को आगे किसी अन्य को किराये पर नहीं दे सकता।
explanation: सबलेटिंग निषेध और पूर्व सहमति की अनिवार्यता संरक्षित।

original: मासिक किराये का भुगतान प्रत्येक माह की 7 तारीख तक अनिवार्य रूप से किया जाएगा।
simplified: हर महीने की 7 तारीख तक किराये का भुगतान करना जरूरी होगा।
explanation: भुगतान तिथि और कर्तव्य संरक्षित।

original: अनुबंध समाप्त करने के लिए दोनों पक्षों में से कोई भी 60 दिन पूर्व लिखित सूचना देगा।
simplified: लीज़ खत्म करने के लिए कोई भी पक्ष 60 दिन पहले लिखित नोटिस जारी कर सकता है।
explanation: समाप्ति हेतु 60 दिन का नोटिस प्रावधान सुरक्षित।

original: मकान खाली करने के 30 दिनों के भीतर सुरक्षा राशि की वापसी वैध कटौती के बाद की जाएगी।
simplified: मकान खाली होने पर 30 दिन में बिजली व टूट-फूट का बकाया काटकर डिपॉजिट लौटाया जाएगा।
explanation: 30 दिन में डिपॉजिट वापसी का प्रावधान अक्षुण्ण।

original: किरायेदार अग्नि सुरक्षा उपकरणों की समय पर जांच व प्रमाणन कराएगा।
simplified: किरायेदार चाहे तो कभी-कभार आग बुझाने वाले सिलिंडर देख सकता है।
explanation: अग्नि सुरक्षा दायित्व को स्वैच्छिक बना दिया गया।

original: सुरक्षा राशि की वापसी परिसर खाली करने के 15 दिनों के भीतर अनिवार्य रूप से होगी।
simplified: सुरक्षा राशि की वापसी मकान खाली करने के 1 वर्ष बाद की जाएगी।
explanation: अवधि 15 दिन से बढ़ाकर 1 वर्ष कर दी गई।

original: मकान पर लगने वाले नगर निगम टैक्स का भुगतान मकान मालिक द्वारा किया जाएगा।
simplified: मकान के सारे म्यूनिसिपल टैक्स और वाटर सेस किरायेदार को भरने होंगे।
explanation: टैक्स देयता मकान मालिक से किरायेदार पर डाली गई।

original: किरायेदार परिसर में किसी भी प्रकार का ज्वलनशील या अवैध पदार्थ नहीं रखेगा।
simplified: किरायेदार को घर के अंदर पेट्रोल व बारूद का गोदाम बनाने की पूरी छूट है।
explanation: सुरक्षा नियम का सीधा उल्लंघन और विलोम।

original: परिसर में पालतू जानवर रखना वर्जित है, सिवाय इसके कि मकान मालिक ने लिखित अनुमति दी हो।

explanation: लिखित अनुमति का वैधानिक अपवाद छोड़ दिया गया।

original: पानी का पाइप फटने जैसी आपात स्थिति में मकान मालिक बिना पूर्व सूचना के प्रवेश कर सकता है।

explanation: आपातकालीन शर्त हटाकर अनियंत्रित प्रवेश अधिकार दिया गया।

original: किरायेदार हर 2 वर्ष में आंतरिक पुताई कराएगा तथा नालियों की सफाई रखेगा।

explanation: पुताई की अवधि व नाली सफाई का दायित्व छोड़ा गया।

original: Rental housing is regulated by states as land, land improvement, and control of rents falls under the State List of the Constitution. Post independence, states regulated rental housing through rent control laws. These laws specified a ceiling on the rental amount, and put conditions for eviction of the tenant, to prevent landlords from charging exorbitant rents and ensure that people found safe and stable housing. The 2015 draft Rental Housing Policy noted that these laws led to low rental yields, and disincentivised landlords from investing in rental properties. These also skewed arrangements towards tenants, made it difficuly to evict them, led to more litigation, and consequently eroded the trust of landlords in the regulatory system.2, This led to the rental demand being serviced through other rental arrangements such as leave and license agreements.2

original: Rental housing is a predominantly urban phenomenon in India. As of 2013, 95% of households in rural areas live in self-owned housing. Globally, the demand for rental housing in urban areas is proportionate to the growth in the population living in urban areas. However, in India the trend has been different, which could be attributed to a policy push towards home ownership and low rental yields.2 Between 1951 and 2011, the urban population in India grew by six times and as of 2011, comprises 31% of the total population.2 However, the share of persons living in urban rental accommodation decreased from 58% to 27% between 1961 and 2011.2

In its judgement, the Court had ruled that requiring Aadhaar card or number may only be made mandatory for expenditure on a subsidy, benefit or service incurred from the Consolidated Fund of India. original: A lease of immovable property is a transfer of a right to enjoy such property, made for a certain time, express or implied, or in perpetuity, in consideration of a price paid or promised, or of money, a share of crops, service or any other thing of value, to be rendered periodically or on specified occasions to the transferor by the transferee, who accepts the transfer on such terms.
simplified: A lease is a legal transfer granting the right to use and enjoy real property for an agreed period or permanently, in return for a lump sum or periodic rent paid by the tenant to the property owner.
explanation: Statutory obligation accurately preserved in plain language (Transfer of Property Act 1882, Section 105).

original: A lease of immovable property is a transfer of a right to enjoy such property, made for a certain time, express or implied, or in perpetuity, in consideration of a price paid or promised, or of money, a share of crops, service or any other thing of value, to be rendered periodically or on specified occasions to the transferor by the transferee, who accepts the transfer on such terms.
simplified: A lease is a voluntary gift transferring full permanent ownership of real property to the tenant without any requirement to pay rent.
explanation: Lease of enjoyment rights inverted into permanent gratuitous ownership transfer.

original: A lease of immovable property is a transfer of a right to enjoy such property, made for a certain time, express or implied, or in perpetuity, in consideration of a price paid or promised, or of money, a share of crops, service or any other thing of value, to be rendered periodically or on specified occasions to the transferor by the transferee, who accepts the transfer on such terms.
simplified: A lease may occasionally allow a person to visit the property if the owner feels like it, without any binding consideration.
explanation: Binding statutory transfer of right reduced to discretionary permission.

original: A lease of immovable property is a transfer of a right to enjoy such property, made for a certain time, express or implied, or in perpetuity, in consideration of a price paid or promised, or of money, a share of crops, service or any other thing of value, to be rendered periodically or on specified occasions to the transferor by the transferee, who accepts the transfer on such terms.
simplified: A lease of immovable property is a transfer of a right to enjoy such property for exactly 99 years only.
explanation: Fixed 99-year limit hallucinated where statute permits any time or perpetuity.

original: In the absence of a contract or local law or usage to the contrary, a lease of immovable property for agricultural or manufacturing purposes shall be deemed to be a lease from year to year, terminable, on the part of either lessor or lessee, by six months' notice.
simplified: Unless a written contract states otherwise, agricultural or manufacturing leases are treated as year-to-year tenancies that either party can terminate by giving six months' notice.
explanation: Statutory obligation accurately preserved in plain language (Transfer of Property Act 1882, Section 106(1)).

original: In the absence of a contract or local law or usage to the contrary, a lease of immovable property for agricultural or manufacturing purposes shall be deemed to be a lease from year to year, terminable, on the part of either lessor or lessee, by six months' notice.
simplified: Unless a written contract states otherwise, agricultural or manufacturing leases are treated as month-to-month tenancies terminable with 15 days' notice.
explanation: Statutory period altered from year-to-year with 6 months notice to month-to-month with 15 days.

original: In the absence of a contract or local law or usage to the contrary, a lease of immovable property for agricultural or manufacturing purposes shall be deemed to be a lease from year to year, terminable, on the part of either lessor or lessee, by six months' notice.
simplified: Agricultural leases can be terminated immediately without any notice period whenever the landlord wishes.
explanation: Mandatory statutory notice condition completely removed.

original: In the absence of a contract or local law or usage to the contrary, a lease of immovable property for agricultural or manufacturing purposes shall be deemed to be a lease from year to year, terminable, on the part of either lessor or lessee, by six months' notice.
simplified: Agricultural leases are year-to-year tenancies which the landlord can terminate by notice, but the tenant has no right to terminate.
explanation: Bilateral termination right stripped from tenant and made unilateral for landlord.

original: A lease of immovable property for any other purpose shall be deemed to be a lease from month to month, terminable, on the part of either lessor or lessee, by fifteen days' notice.
simplified: Unless agreed otherwise, leases for residential or commercial purposes are considered month-to-month tenancies that either landlord or tenant can end with 15 days' notice.
explanation: Statutory obligation accurately preserved in plain language (Transfer of Property Act 1882, Section 106(2)).

original: The lessee is bound to pay or tender, at the proper time and place, the premium or rent to the lessor or his agent in this behalf.

simplified: Landlords and tenants may optionally write an agreement if they want to, but oral leases are equally valid.
explanation: Strict statutory prohibition softened to optional preference.

original: Notwithstanding anything contained in any other law for the time being in force, no person shall, after the commencement of this Act, let or take on rent any premises except by an agreement in writing.
simplified: No person shall let property except under an agreement.
explanation: Omitted the explicit 'in writing' requirement and non-obstante clause.

original: The tenancy agreement shall be jointly submitted by the landlord and the tenant to the Rent Authority within a period of two months from the date of tenancy agreement.
simplified: The landlord and tenant must jointly report and submit the rental agreement to the Rent Authority within two months of signing it.
explanation: Statutory obligation accurately preserved in plain language (Model Tenancy Act 2021, Section 4(2)).

original: The tenancy agreement shall be jointly submitted by the landlord and the tenant to the Rent Authority within a period of two months from the date of tenancy agreement.
simplified: The rental agreement must be submitted to the Rent Authority within two years of signing.
explanation: Statutory submission timeline distorted from 2 months to 2 years.

original: The tenancy agreement shall be jointly submitted by the landlord and the tenant to the Rent Authority within a period of two months from the date of tenancy agreement.
simplified: Only the tenant is required to submit the rental agreement, and the landlord has no obligation.
explanation: Joint submission duty reduced unilaterally to tenant.

original: The tenancy agreement shall be jointly submitted by the landlord and the tenant to the Rent Authority within a period of two months from the date of tenancy agreement.
simplified: The parties may optionally submit the agreement to the Rent Authority if they wish to pay registration fees.
explanation: Mandatory reporting converted to discretionary choice.

original: Every tenancy entered into after the commencement of this Act shall be valid for a period as agreed upon between the landlord and the tenant and as specified in the tenancy agreement.
simplified: Every new tenancy under this Act remains valid for the exact duration agreed upon and specified in the written agreement.
explanation: Statutory obligation accurately preserved in plain language (Model Tenancy Act 2021, Section 5(1)).

original: Every tenancy entered into after the commencement of this Act shall be valid for a period as agreed upon between the landlord and the tenant and as specified in the tenancy agreement.
simplified: All tenancies entered under the Act are automatically permanent and cannot be limited to an agreed period.
explanation: Fixed agreed duration inverted into mandatory permanent tenure.

original: Every tenancy entered into after the commencement of this Act shall be valid for a period as agreed upon between the landlord and the tenant and as specified in the tenancy agreement.
simplified: Every tenancy is valid for a period specified in the agreement.
explanation: Minor stylistic compression preserving essential validity rule.

original: If a tenancy for a fixed term ends and has not been renewed or the tenant fails to vacate the premises at the end of such tenancy, the tenant shall be liable to pay an enhanced rent to the landlord as specified in section 23.
simplified: If a tenant fails to vacate or renew after a fixed-term lease ends, they must pay higher penalty rent as prescribed under Section 23.
explanation: Statutory obligation accurately preserved in plain language (Model Tenancy Act 2021, Section 5(3)).

original: If a tenancy for a fixed term ends and has not been renewed or the tenant fails to vacate the premises at the end of such tenancy, the tenant shall be liable to pay an enhanced rent to the landlord as specified in section 23.
simplified: If a tenant refuses to vacate after lease expiry, they are entitled to a 50 percent discount on future rent.
explanation: Penalty enhanced rent flipped into rent discount.

original: If a tenancy for a fixed term ends and has not been renewed or the tenant fails to vacate the premises at the end of such tenancy, the tenant shall be liable to pay an enhanced rent to the landlord as specified in section 23.
simplified: A tenant who does not vacate must pay regular rent with no penalty of any kind.
explanation: Statutory enhanced penalty liability erased.

original: If a tenancy for a fixed term ends and has not been renewed or the tenant fails to vacate the premises at the end of such tenancy, the tenant shall be liable to pay an enhanced rent to the landlord as specified in section 23.
simplified: The tenant shall be liable to pay rent.
explanation: Omitted lease expiry trigger and statutory enhanced rate.

original: No tenant shall sublet whole or any part of the premises held by him as a tenant, or transfer or assign his rights in the tenancy agreement or any part thereof, except on entering into a supplementary agreement to the existing tenancy agreement with the landlord.
simplified: A tenant cannot sublet any part of the property or transfer their tenancy rights without executing a supplementary written agreement with the landlord.
explanation: Statutory obligation accurately preserved in plain language (Model Tenancy Act 2021, Section 7).

original: No tenant shall sublet whole or any part of the premises held by him as a tenant, or transfer or assign his rights in the tenancy agreement or any part thereof, except on entering into a supplementary agreement to the existing tenancy agreement with the landlord.
simplified: A tenant has the unrestricted right to sublet the entire apartment to third parties without informing the landlord.
explanation: Subletting ban reversed into unrestricted subletting right.

original: No tenant shall sublet whole or any part of the premises held by him as a tenant, or transfer or assign his rights in the tenancy agreement or any part thereof, except on entering into a supplementary agreement to the existing tenancy agreement with the landlord.
simplified: A tenant can sublet if they verbally notify the building security guard.
explanation: Requirement of supplementary agreement with landlord degraded to verbal guard notice.

original: No tenant shall sublet whole or any part of the premises held by him as a tenant, or transfer or assign his rights in the tenancy agreement or any part thereof, except on entering into a supplementary agreement to the existing tenancy agreement with the landlord.
simplified: A tenant cannot sublease the property.
explanation: Omitted exception permitting sublease via supplementary agreement.

original: The rent payable in respect of the premises shall be the rent agreed upon between the landlord and the tenant under the tenancy agreement.
simplified: The rent for the premises is determined entirely by mutual agreement between the landlord and tenant as stated in their contract.
explanation: Statutory obligation accurately preserved in plain language (Model Tenancy Act 2021, Section 8).

original: The rent payable in respect of the premises shall be the rent agreed upon between the landlord and the tenant under the tenancy agreement.
simplified: Rent is fixed unilaterally by the local municipal corporator regardless of the agreement.
explanation: Contractual agreement substituted with third-party municipal fiat.

original: The rent payable in respect of the premises shall be the rent agreed upon between the landlord and the tenant under the tenancy agreement.
simplified: The rent is the amount agreed between landlord and tenant.
explanation: Concise plain reformulation preserving core principle.

original: Revision of rent between the landlord and the tenant shall be in accordance with the terms of the tenancy agreement.
simplified: Rent increases or adjustments must strictly follow the terms and conditions agreed in the tenancy contract.
explanation: Statutory obligation accurately preserved in plain language (Model Tenancy Act 2021, Section 9(1)).

original: Revision of rent between the landlord and the tenant shall be in accordance with the terms of the tenancy agreement.
simplified: The landlord can double the rent at any time without following any agreement terms.
explanation: Rent revision contract terms disregarded in favor of arbitrary hikes.

original: Revision of rent between the landlord and the tenant shall be in accordance with the terms of the tenancy agreement.
simplified: Rent revision shall follow the agreement terms.
explanation: Direct plain rephrasing.

original: The landlord shall give a notice in writing to the tenant, three months before the revised rent becomes due, of his intention to increase the rent.
simplified: A landlord must provide written notice at least three months in advance before any revised rent takes effect.
explanation: Statutory obligation accurately preserved in plain language (Model Tenancy Act 2021, Section 9(2)).

original: The landlord shall give a notice in writing to the tenant, three months before the revised rent becomes due, of his intention to increase the rent.
simplified: A landlord can increase rent immediately without giving any advance written notice.
explanation: Three-month advance notice condition erased.

original: The landlord shall give a notice in writing to the tenant, three months before the revised rent becomes due, of his intention to increase the rent.
simplified: A landlord must give 12 months' advance notice before revising rent.
explanation: Notice period altered from 3 months to 12 months.

original: The landlord shall give a notice in writing to the tenant, three months before the revised rent becomes due, of his intention to increase the rent.
simplified: The landlord must inform the tenant before rent increases.
explanation: Omitted three-month statutory timeline and written requirement.

original: The security deposit to be paid by the tenant in advance shall not exceed two months' rent in case of residential premises, and six months' rent in case of non-residential premises.
simplified: The security deposit payable by a tenant is capped at a maximum of two months' rent for homes, and six months' rent for commercial spaces.
explanation: Statutory obligation accurately preserved in plain language (Model Tenancy Act 2021, Section 11(1)).

original: The security deposit to be paid by the tenant in advance shall not exceed two months' rent in case of residential premises, and six months' rent in case of non-residential premises.
simplified: Landlords can demand up to five years of advance rent as security deposit for residential apartments.
explanation: Statutory cap distorted from 2 months to 5 years.

original: The security deposit to be paid by the tenant in advance shall not exceed two months' rent in case of residential premises, and six months' rent in case of non-residential premises.
simplified: The security deposit is capped at six months' rent for residential homes and two months' rent for commercial shops.
explanation: Caps swapped between residential and commercial premises.

original: The security deposit to be paid by the tenant in advance shall not exceed two months' rent in case of residential premises, and six months' rent in case of non-residential premises.
simplified: Security deposit cannot exceed statutory caps.
explanation: Omitted the explicit 2-month residential and 6-month commercial limits.

original: The security deposit shall be refunded to the tenant on vacating the premises, after making due deductions of any liability relating to rent or damages caused by the tenant.
simplified: The security deposit must be returned to the tenant upon handover of the property, minus legitimate deductions for unpaid rent or tenant-caused damage.
explanation: Statutory obligation accurately preserved in plain language (Model Tenancy Act 2021, Section 11(2)).

original: The security deposit shall be refunded to the tenant on vacating the premises, after making due deductions of any liability relating to rent or damages caused by the tenant.
simplified: The landlord is legally permitted to keep the entire security deposit as non-refundable profit upon vacation.
explanation: Deposit refund duty converted to non-refundable retention.

original: The security deposit shall be refunded to the tenant on vacating the premises, after making due deductions of any liability relating to rent or damages caused by the tenant.
simplified: The security deposit shall be refunded within five years after the tenant vacates.
explanation: Timeline extended to 5 years.

original: The security deposit shall be refunded to the tenant on vacating the premises, after making due deductions of any liability relating to rent or damages caused by the tenant.
simplified: The deposit must be returned with zero deductions even if the tenant owes months of rent and broke all fixtures.
explanation: Legitimate deduction proviso completely removed.

original: Every tenant shall be entitled to obtain an acknowledgement receipt for any amount paid to the landlord on account of rent or security deposit.
simplified: Tenants have a statutory right to receive a written payment receipt for any rent or security deposit paid to the landlord.
explanation: Statutory obligation accurately preserved in plain language (Model Tenancy Act 2021, Section 13).

original: Every tenant shall be entitled to obtain an acknowledgement receipt for any amount paid to the landlord on account of rent or security deposit.
simplified: Landlords are expressly forbidden from providing receipts for any cash rent received.
explanation: Right to receipt converted to prohibition against receipts.

original: Every tenant shall be entitled to obtain an acknowledgement receipt for any amount paid to the landlord on account of rent or security deposit.
simplified: The tenant may request a receipt if the landlord feels willing to provide one.
explanation: Enforceable right converted to discretionary courtesy.

original: Every tenant shall be entitled to obtain an acknowledgement receipt for any amount paid to the landlord on account of rent or security deposit.
simplified: Tenants are entitled to receipts for payments.
explanation: Concise plain summary.

original: The tenant shall keep the premises in good condition and shall take reasonable care in using the premises and shall not cause intentional or negligent damage to the premises.
simplified: The tenant must maintain the premises in good order, use it prudently, and avoid intentional or negligent damage.
explanation: Statutory obligation accurately preserved in plain language (Model Tenancy Act 2021, Section 15(1)).

original: The tenant shall keep the premises in good condition and shall take reasonable care in using the premises and shall not cause intentional or negligent damage to the premises.
simplified: The tenant is entitled to inflict intentional damage on the premises without any responsibility.
explanation: Direct inversion of duty of care into right to vandalize.

original: The tenant shall keep the premises in good condition and shall take reasonable care in using the premises and shall not cause intentional or negligent damage to the premises.
simplified: The tenant shall keep the premises in reasonable condition.
explanation: Slight plain simplification.

original: In case of any damage caused to the premises due to negligence of the tenant, the tenant shall be liable to make good the damage or reimburse the landlord for the cost of repair.
simplified: If the tenant damages the property through negligence, they must either repair the damage or compensate the landlord for the repair costs.
explanation: Statutory obligation accurately preserved in plain language (Model Tenancy Act 2021, Section 15(3)).

original: In case of any damage caused to the premises due to negligence of the tenant, the tenant shall be liable to make good the damage or reimburse the landlord for the cost of repair.
simplified: The landlord must pay for all damages caused by the tenant's drunken negligence with no right to reimbursement.
explanation: Liability inverted from tenant to landlord.

original: In case of any damage caused to the premises due to negligence of the tenant, the tenant shall be liable to make good the damage or reimburse the landlord for the cost of repair.
simplified: The tenant may consider whether to fix damage caused by negligence.
explanation: Mandatory liability softened to discretionary option.

original: The landlord shall be responsible for structural repairs, whitewashing of walls and painting of doors and windows at reasonable intervals as agreed between the parties.
simplified: The landlord is responsible for structural repairs, interior/exterior whitewashing, and painting doors and windows at agreed intervals.
explanation: Statutory obligation accurately preserved in plain language (Model Tenancy Act 2021, Section 16(1)).

original: The landlord shall be responsible for structural repairs, whitewashing of walls and painting of doors and windows at reasonable intervals as agreed between the parties.
simplified: The tenant must bear full cost of structural wall rebuilding and exterior building repainting.
explanation: Structural maintenance duty shifted to tenant.

original: The landlord shall be responsible for structural repairs, whitewashing of walls and painting of doors and windows at reasonable intervals as agreed between the parties.
simplified: The landlord may occasionally paint doors if requested.
explanation: Duty softened to optional courtesy.

original: The landlord shall be responsible for structural repairs, whitewashing of walls and painting of doors and windows at reasonable intervals as agreed between the parties.
simplified: The landlord handles structural maintenance and painting.
explanation: Plain plain-language summary.

original: The landlord or property manager shall not enter the premises without giving a prior notice of twenty-four hours in writing or through electronic mode to the tenant, and such entry shall be only during sunrise and sunset.
simplified: A landlord or property manager cannot enter the rented home without giving at least 24 hours' prior written or digital notice, and entry is restricted to daytime hours.
explanation: Statutory obligation accurately preserved in plain language (Model Tenancy Act 2021, Section 17).

original: The landlord or property manager shall not enter the premises without giving a prior notice of twenty-four hours in writing or through electronic mode to the tenant, and such entry shall be only during sunrise and sunset.
simplified: The landlord can unlock the doors and enter the apartment at midnight unannounced without giving any notice.
explanation: Privacy safeguards violated in both notice and time restrictions.

original: The landlord or property manager shall not enter the premises without giving a prior notice of twenty-four hours in writing or through electronic mode to the tenant, and such entry shall be only during sunrise and sunset.
simplified: The landlord must give at least three weeks' prior notice before entering for routine inspection.
explanation: Notice period distorted from 24 hours to 3 weeks.

original: The landlord or property manager shall not enter the premises without giving a prior notice of twenty-four hours in writing or through electronic mode to the tenant, and such entry shall be only during sunrise and sunset.
simplified: The landlord may enter the apartment during daytime.
explanation: Omitted mandatory 24-hour advance notice requirement.

original: No landlord or property manager shall, either by himself or through any other person, withhold any essential supply or service in respect of the premises occupied by the tenant.
simplified: Landlords and property managers are strictly prohibited from cutting off essential services like water, electricity, or sanitation to force a tenant out.
explanation: Statutory obligation accurately preserved in plain language (Model Tenancy Act 2021, Section 20).

original: No landlord or property manager shall, either by himself or through any other person, withhold any essential supply or service in respect of the premises occupied by the tenant.
simplified: The landlord is fully authorized to disconnect water and electricity to compel the tenant to pay rent.
explanation: Direct inversion of statutory prohibition against cutting utilities.

original: No landlord or property manager shall, either by himself or through any other person, withhold any essential supply or service in respect of the premises occupied by the tenant.
simplified: The landlord should avoid disconnecting electricity if possible.
explanation: Absolute statutory bar softened to discretionary guidance.

original: No landlord or property manager shall, either by himself or through any other person, withhold any essential supply or service in respect of the premises occupied by the tenant.
simplified: No person shall cut off essential services.
explanation: Plain language reformulation.

original: The Rent Court may make an order for recovery of possession of the premises on the ground that the tenant has failed to pay the agreed rent for more than two consecutive months.
simplified: The Rent Court can order eviction if the tenant fails to pay the agreed rent for more than two consecutive months.
explanation: Statutory obligation accurately preserved in plain language (Model Tenancy Act 2021, Section 21(2)(a)).

original: The Rent Court may make an order for recovery of possession of the premises on the ground that the tenant has failed to pay the agreed rent for more than two consecutive months.
simplified: The Rent Court can evict a tenant who pays rent on time every single month.
explanation: Eviction ground inverted against compliant tenants.

original: The Rent Court may make an order for recovery of possession of the premises on the ground that the tenant has failed to pay the agreed rent for more than two consecutive months.
simplified: Eviction for rent default can only occur if rent remains unpaid for more than two consecutive years.
explanation: Default threshold distorted from 2 months to 2 years.

original: The Rent Court may make an order for recovery of possession of the premises on the ground that the tenant has failed to pay the agreed rent for more than two consecutive months.
simplified: The Rent Court may evict for unpaid rent.
explanation: Omitted the statutory requirement of two consecutive months of default.

original: The Rent Court may order eviction if the tenant has parted with the possession of whole or any part of the premises without obtaining the written consent of the landlord.
simplified: A tenant can be legally evicted if they sublet or give up possession of part or all of the premises without written consent from the landlord.
explanation: Statutory obligation accurately preserved in plain language (Model Tenancy Act 2021, Section 21(2)(b)).

original: The Rent Court may order eviction if the tenant has parted with the possession of whole or any part of the premises without obtaining the written consent of the landlord.
simplified: A tenant who sublets without consent is rewarded with an automatic extension of the lease.
explanation: Eviction ground converted into statutory reward.

original: The Rent Court may order eviction if the tenant has parted with the possession of whole or any part of the premises without obtaining the written consent of the landlord.
simplified: A tenant can sublet without consent as long as they inform their roommate.
explanation: Requirement of landlord written consent omitted and replaced with roommate notice.

original: The Rent Court may order eviction if the tenant has parted with the possession of whole or any part of the premises without obtaining the written consent of the landlord.
simplified: Eviction is permitted if the tenant sublets without written consent.
explanation: Accurate plain legal reformulation.

original: The Rent Court may order eviction where the tenant has continued misuse of the premises even after receipt of a notice from the landlord to desist from such misuse.
simplified: Eviction can be granted if the tenant continues using the property for unauthorized or harmful purposes after receiving a formal cease-and-desist notice.
explanation: Statutory obligation accurately preserved in plain language (Model Tenancy Act 2021, Section 21(2)(d)).

original: The Rent Court may order eviction where the tenant has continued misuse of the premises even after receipt of a notice from the landlord to desist from such misuse.
simplified: The landlord can evict immediately for misuse without serving any prior warning notice to stop.
explanation: Notice to desist prerequisite removed.

original: The Rent Court may order eviction where the tenant has continued misuse of the premises even after receipt of a notice from the landlord to desist from such misuse.
simplified: A tenant has the right to misuse premises despite notices.
explanation: Ground of eviction inverted into entitlement.

original: The Rent Court may order eviction where the tenant has continued misuse of the premises even after receipt of a notice from the landlord to desist from such misuse.
simplified: Misuse of premises permits eviction.
explanation: Omitted notice to desist requirement.

original: Where the tenant fails to vacate the premises on the determination of the tenancy, the tenant shall be liable to pay to the landlord compensation of double the monthly rent for the first two months, and four times the monthly rent thereafter, until he vacates the premises.
simplified: A tenant who refuses to vacate after lease termination must pay compensation of double rent for the first two months, and quadruple rent for each subsequent month until possession is surrendered.
explanation: Statutory obligation accurately preserved in plain language (Model Tenancy Act 2021, Section 23).

original: Where the tenant fails to vacate the premises on the determination of the tenancy, the tenant shall be liable to pay to the landlord compensation of double the monthly rent for the first two months, and four times the monthly rent thereafter, until he vacates the premises.
simplified: A tenant who refuses to leave after the lease ends pays half the normal rent until they decide to vacate.
explanation: Punitive rent multipliers converted into discounted rent.

original: Where the tenant fails to vacate the premises on the determination of the tenancy, the tenant shall be liable to pay to the landlord compensation of double the monthly rent for the first two months, and four times the monthly rent thereafter, until he vacates the premises.
simplified: A tenant who overstays must pay ten times the rent for the first two months and fifty times thereafter.
explanation: Exaggerated numerical multipliers beyond statutory formula.

original: Where the tenant fails to vacate the premises on the determination of the tenancy, the tenant shall be liable to pay to the landlord compensation of double the monthly rent for the first two months, and four times the monthly rent thereafter, until he vacates the premises.
simplified: The tenant must pay double rent for 2 months and four times rent thereafter if they fail to vacate.
explanation: Faithful plain simplification.

original: The District Collector shall, with the previous approval of the State Government, appoint an officer, not below the rank of Deputy Collector, to be the Rent Authority for the area within his jurisdiction.
simplified: The District Collector, with State Government approval, appoints an officer of at least Deputy Collector rank to serve as the local Rent Authority.
explanation: Statutory obligation accurately preserved in plain language (Model Tenancy Act 2021, Section 30).

original: The District Collector shall, with the previous approval of the State Government, appoint an officer, not below the rank of Deputy Collector, to be the Rent Authority for the area within his jurisdiction.
simplified: Any private security agency can appoint themselves as the official Rent Authority for the district.
explanation: Official statutory appointment power outsourced to private security.

original: The District Collector shall, with the previous approval of the State Government, appoint an officer, not below the rank of Deputy Collector, to be the Rent Authority for the area within his jurisdiction.
simplified: The Rent Authority must be an officer of at least Deputy Collector rank.
explanation: Direct summary.

original: No civil court shall have jurisdiction to entertain any suit or proceeding in respect of any matter to which the provisions of this Act apply.
simplified: Civil courts are barred from hearing cases or lawsuits relating to tenancy matters governed by this Act, which fall exclusively under Rent Courts and Tribunals.
explanation: Statutory obligation accurately preserved in plain language (Model Tenancy Act 2021, Section 38).

original: No civil court shall have jurisdiction to entertain any suit or proceeding in respect of any matter to which the provisions of this Act apply.
simplified: All tenancy disputes must be filed exclusively in ordinary civil courts and Rent Courts are abolished.
explanation: Jurisdictional bar completely inverted.

original: No civil court shall have jurisdiction to entertain any suit or proceeding in respect of any matter to which the provisions of this Act apply.
simplified: Civil courts may optionally hear tenancy disputes if parties prefer.
explanation: Strict jurisdictional exclusion demoted to optional concurrent forum.

original: The Controller may make an order for the recovery of possession of the premises on the ground that the tenant has neither paid nor tendered the whole of the arrears of rent legally recoverable from him within two months of the date on which a notice of demand for the arrears of rent has been served on him by the landlord.
simplified: A tenant can be evicted if they fail to pay the full legal rent arrears within two months of receiving a formal written demand notice from the landlord.
explanation: Statutory obligation accurately preserved in plain language (Delhi Rent Control Act 1958, Section 14(1)(a)).

original: The Controller may make an order for the recovery of possession of the premises on the ground that the tenant has neither paid nor tendered the whole of the arrears of rent legally recoverable from him within two months of the date on which a notice of demand for the arrears of rent has been served on him by the landlord.
simplified: A tenant can be evicted immediately without the landlord ever sending a notice of demand.
explanation: Eliminated mandatory statutory notice of demand.

original: The Controller may make an order for the recovery of possession of the premises on the ground that the tenant has neither paid nor tendered the whole of the arrears of rent legally recoverable from him within two months of the date on which a notice of demand for the arrears of rent has been served on him by the landlord.
simplified: The tenant must pay arrears within 24 hours of receiving notice or face instant eviction.
explanation: Notice period slashed from 2 months to 24 hours.

original: The Controller may make an order for the recovery of possession of the premises on the ground that the tenant has neither paid nor tendered the whole of the arrears of rent legally recoverable from him within two months of the date on which a notice of demand for the arrears of rent has been served on him by the landlord.
simplified: The landlord can evict if arrears are not paid after demand notice.
explanation: Omitted statutory two-month grace period.

original: The Controller may order eviction if the premises let for residential purposes are required bona fide by the landlord for occupation as a residence for himself or for any member of his family dependent on him.
simplified: The Rent Controller can grant eviction if the landlord genuinely and in good faith requires the residential property for personal or dependent family residence.
explanation: Statutory obligation accurately preserved in plain language (Delhi Rent Control Act 1958, Section 14(1)(e)).

original: The Controller may order eviction if the premises let for residential purposes are required bona fide by the landlord for occupation as a residence for himself or for any member of his family dependent on him.
simplified: The landlord can evict the tenant by falsely pretending to need the home for personal residence when they intend to re-rent at higher price.
explanation: Bona fide requirement subverted to endorse bad-faith pretextual eviction.

original: The Controller may order eviction if the premises let for residential purposes are required bona fide by the landlord for occupation as a residence for himself or for any member of his family dependent on him.
simplified: Eviction for personal residence is completely barred even if the landlord has nowhere else to live.
explanation: Statutory eviction ground for bona fide need extinguished.

original: The Controller may order eviction if the premises let for residential purposes are required bona fide by the landlord for occupation as a residence for himself or for any member of his family dependent on him.
simplified: The landlord can evict if premises are required for residence.
explanation: Omitted the critical 'bona fide' and dependent family qualifications.

original: Where a landlord recovers possession of any premises from the tenant on the ground of bona fide requirement, the landlord shall not, except with the permission of the Controller, let the whole or any part of the premises within three years from the date of obtaining possession.
simplified: If a landlord evicts a tenant for personal residence, they are forbidden from re-letting the property to anyone else for three years without the Controller's permission.
explanation: Statutory obligation accurately preserved in plain language (Delhi Rent Control Act 1958, Section 19(1)).

original: Where a landlord recovers possession of any premises from the tenant on the ground of bona fide requirement, the landlord shall not, except with the permission of the Controller, let the whole or any part of the premises within three years from the date of obtaining possession.
simplified: A landlord who evicts for personal residence can immediately re-let the property the next day at higher rent with no penalty.
explanation: Statutory anti-speculation safeguard reversed.

original: Where a landlord recovers possession of any premises from the tenant on the ground of bona fide requirement, the landlord shall not, except with the permission of the Controller, let the whole or any part of the premises within three years from the date of obtaining possession.
simplified: The landlord cannot re-let the premises for three months after obtaining possession.
explanation: Restriction period reduced from 3 years to 3 months.

original: Where a landlord recovers possession of any premises from the tenant on the ground of bona fide requirement, the landlord shall not, except with the permission of the Controller, let the whole or any part of the premises within three years from the date of obtaining possession.
simplified: The landlord cannot re-let without permission for three years.
explanation: Plain reformulation.

original: A landlord shall not be entitled to the recovery of possession of any premises so long as the tenant pays, or is ready and willing to pay, the amount of the standard rent and permitted increases, if any, and observes and performs the other conditions of the tenancy.
simplified: A landlord cannot evict a tenant so long as the tenant pays standard rent and permitted increases and abides by the lease conditions.
explanation: Statutory obligation accurately preserved in plain language (Maharashtra Rent Control Act 1999, Section 15(1)).

original: A landlord shall not be entitled to the recovery of possession of any premises so long as the tenant pays, or is ready and willing to pay, the amount of the standard rent and permitted increases, if any, and observes and performs the other conditions of the tenancy.
simplified: A landlord can evict any tenant at will even if the tenant pays full rent and fulfills every condition.
explanation: Core statutory protection against arbitrary eviction eliminated.

original: A landlord shall not be entitled to the recovery of possession of any premises so long as the tenant pays, or is ready and willing to pay, the amount of the standard rent and permitted increases, if any, and observes and performs the other conditions of the tenancy.
simplified: The tenant is protected from eviction so long as rent is paid.
explanation: Omitted requirement to observe other lease conditions.

original: No landlord shall, without just or sufficient cause, cut off or withhold any essential supply or service enjoyed by the tenant in respect of the premises let to him.
simplified: A landlord is strictly forbidden from cutting off or disrupting water, electricity, or other essential services enjoyed by the tenant without lawful justification.
explanation: Statutory obligation accurately preserved in plain language (Maharashtra Rent Control Act 1999, Section 29).

original: No landlord shall, without just or sufficient cause, cut off or withhold any essential supply or service enjoyed by the tenant in respect of the premises let to him.
simplified: The landlord can cut off electricity and drinking water whenever rent is slightly delayed.
explanation: Utility protection inverted into authorized harassment weapon.

original: No landlord shall, without just or sufficient cause, cut off or withhold any essential supply or service enjoyed by the tenant in respect of the premises let to him.
simplified: Landlords should try not to disconnect essential services.
explanation: Prohibition downgraded to optional suggestion.

original: स्थावर सम्पत्ति का पट्टा ऐसी सम्पत्ति के उपभोग करने के अधिकार का ऐसा अन्तरण है जो एक निश्चित समय के लिए या शाश्वत काल के लिए, किसी कीमत या आवधिक रूप से देय भाटक के प्रतिफल के बदले किया जाता है, जिसे अन्तरिती स्वीकार करता है।

original: स्थावर सम्पत्ति का पट्टा ऐसी सम्पत्ति के उपभोग करने के अधिकार का ऐसा अन्तरण है जो एक निश्चित समय के लिए या शाश्वत काल के लिए, किसी कीमत या आवधिक रूप से देय भाटक के प्रतिफल के बदले किया जाता है, जिसे अन्तरिती स्वीकार करता है।

original: किसी संविदा या स्थानीय विधि या रूढ़ि के अभाव में, कृषि या विनिर्माण के प्रयोजनों के लिए स्थावर सम्पत्ति का पट्टा वर्षानुवर्षी पट्टा समझा जाएगा, जो किसी भी पक्षकार द्वारा छह मास की लिखित सूचना द्वारा समाप्त किया जा सकेगा।

explanation: सटीक वैधानिक विधिक दायित्व व अधिकारों का स्पष्ट हिंदी में संरक्षण (सम्पत्ति अन्तरण अधिनियम 1882, धारा 106(1))।

original: किसी संविदा या स्थानीय विधि या रूढ़ि के अभाव में, कृषि या विनिर्माण के प्रयोजनों के लिए स्थावर सम्पत्ति का पट्टा वर्षानुवर्षी पट्टा समझा जाएगा, जो किसी भी पक्षकार द्वारा छह मास की लिखित सूचना द्वारा समाप्त किया जा सकेगा।

explanation: छह मास की विधिक अवधि घटाकर 15 दिन कर दी गई।

original: किसी संविदा या स्थानीय विधि या रूढ़ि के अभाव में, कृषि या विनिर्माण के प्रयोजनों के लिए स्थावर सम्पत्ति का पट्टा वर्षानुवर्षी पट्टा समझा जाएगा, जो किसी भी पक्षकार द्वारा छह मास की लिखित सूचना द्वारा समाप्त किया जा सकेगा।

explanation: अनिवार्य सूचना की विधिक शर्त हटा दी गई।

original: किसी संविदा या स्थानीय विधि या रूढ़ि के अभाव में, कृषि या विनिर्माण के प्रयोजनों के लिए स्थावर सम्पत्ति का पट्टा वर्षानुवर्षी पट्टा समझा जाएगा, जो किसी भी पक्षकार द्वारा छह मास की लिखित सूचना द्वारा समाप्त किया जा सकेगा।
simplified: मकान मालिक नोटिस दे सकता है लेकिन किराएदार को लीज समाप्त करने का कोई अधिकार नहीं होगा।
explanation: पक्षकारों के द्विपक्षीय अधिकार को एकतरफा बना दिया गया।

original: किसी अन्य प्रयोजन के लिए स्थावर सम्पत्ति का पट्टा मासानुमासी पट्टा समझा जाएगा, जो पट्टाकर्ता या पट्टेदार द्वारा पन्द्रह दिन की सूचना द्वारा समाप्त किया जा सकेगा।
simplified: अन्य किसी उद्देश्य (जैसे आवास या दुकान) के लिए पट्टा महीने-दर-महीने का माना जाएगा, जिसे दोनों में से कोई भी पक्ष 15 दिन का नोटिस देकर खत्म कर सकता है।

original: किसी अन्य प्रयोजन के लिए स्थावर सम्पत्ति का पट्टा मासानुमासी पट्टा समझा जाएगा, जो पट्टाकर्ता या पट्टेदार द्वारा पन्द्रह दिन की सूचना द्वारा समाप्त किया जा सकेगा।

simplified: किराएदार को 15 दिन में निकाला जा सकता है भले ही उसने कोई गलती न की हो लेकिन किराएदार कभी खुद खाली नहीं कर सकता।

explanation: सटीक वैधानिक विधिक दायित्व व अधिकारों का स्पष्ट हिंदी में संरक्षण (सम्पत्ति अन्तरण अधिनियम 1882, धारा 107)।

original: स्थावर सम्पत्ति का वर्षानुवर्षी पट्टा या एक वर्ष से अधिक की किसी कालावधि का पट्टा केवल रजिस्ट्रीकृत लिखत द्वारा ही किया जा सकता है।

original: पट्टाकर्ता पट्टेदार को सम्पत्ति में के ऐसे किसी तात्त्विक दोष को प्रकट करने के लिए आबद्ध है जिससे पट्टाकर्ता अवगत है और पट्टेदार सामान्य सावधानी से उसका पता नहीं लगा सकता।

original: पट्टाकर्ता पट्टेदार को सम्पत्ति में के ऐसे किसी तात्त्विक दोष को प्रकट करने के लिए आबद्ध है जिससे पट्टाकर्ता अवगत है और पट्टेदार सामान्य सावधानी से उसका पता नहीं लगा सकता।

original: पट्टेदार द्वारा प्रार्थना किए जाने पर पट्टाकर्ता उसे सम्पत्ति का कब्जा सौंपने के लिए आबद्ध है।

original: यदि पट्टेदार पट्टे द्वारा आरक्षित भाटक का संदाय करता रहे और अपने संविदात्मक दायित्वों का पालन करे, तो वह पट्टे की अवधि के दौरान बिना किसी बाधा के सम्पत्ति का उपभोग कर सकेगा।

original: जहाँ पट्टा भाटक का संदाय न करने के कारण समपहृत हुआ है और पट्टाकर्ता बेदखली का वाद लाता है, वहाँ यदि पट्टेदार वाद की सुनवाई के समय बकाया भाटक, ब्याज और वाद का समस्त खर्च संदत्त कर दे, तो न्यायालय पट्टेदार को समपहरण से अनुतोष प्रदान कर सकेगा।

original: जहाँ पट्टा भाटक का संदाय न करने के कारण समपहृत हुआ है और पट्टाकर्ता बेदखली का वाद लाता है, वहाँ यदि पट्टेदार वाद की सुनवाई के समय बकाया भाटक, ब्याज और वाद का समस्त खर्च संदत्त कर दे, तो न्यायालय पट्टेदार को समपहरण से अनुतोष प्रदान कर सकेगा।

Post independence, states regulated rental housing through rent control laws. These laws specified a ceiling on the rental amount, and put conditions for eviction of the tenant, to prevent landlords from charging exorbitant rents and ensure that people found safe and stable housing. The 2015 draft Rental Housing Policy noted that these laws led to low rental yields, and disincentivised landlords from investing in rental properties. original: Rental housing is a predominantly urban phenomenon in India. As of 2013, 95% of households in rural areas live in self-owned housing. However, in India the trend has been different, which could be attributed to a policy push towards home ownership and low rental yields.2 Between 1951 and 2011, the urban population in India grew by six times and as of 2011, comprises 31% of the total population.2 However, the share of persons living in urban rental accommodation decreased from 58% to 27% between 1961 and 2011.2
simplified: Rental housing is a predominantly urban phenomenon in India. As of 2023, 95% of households in rural areas live in self-owned housing. Globally, the demand for rental housing in urban areas is proportionate to the growth in the population living in urban areas. However, in India the trend has been different, which could be attributed to a policy push towards home ownership and low rental yields.2 Between 1951 and 2011, the urban population in India grew by six times and as of 2011, comprises 31% of the total population.2 However, the share of persons living in urban rental accommodation decreased from 58% to 27% between 1961 and 2011.2
explanation: Numerical threshold distorted from 2013 to 2023.

original: Tenancy agreement: The Model Act states that to rent any premises, a written agreement must be signed between the landlord and the tenant. The agreement must specify: (i) the rent payable, (ii) the time period for the tenancy, (iii) terms and period for revision of rent, (iv) the security deposit to be paid in advance, (v) reasonable causes for entry of landlord into the premises, and (vi) responsibilities to maintain premises. The Rent Authority must be intimated about the agreement within two months from the date of agreement. This will apply to all premises used for residential, commercial, and educational purposes.
simplified: Tenancy agreement: The Model Act states that to rent any rental property, a written agreement must be signed between the lessor or property owner and the lessee. The agreement must specify: (i) the rent payable, (ii) the time period for the tenancy, (iii) terms and period for revision of rent, (iv) the security deposit to be paid in advance, (v) reasonable causes for entry of landlord into the rental property, and (vi) responsibilities to maintain rental property. The Rent Authority must be intimated about the agreement within two months from the date of agreement. This will apply to all rental property used for residential, commercial, and educational purposes.
explanation: Lexical synonym reformulation preserving identical statutory obligation.

original: Security deposit: The security deposit may not exceed: (i) two months’ rent for residential premises, and (ii) six-months’ rent for non-residential premises. The security deposit will be refunded by the landlord to the tenant at the time of taking over vacant possession of the premises, after making due deductions.
simplified: Security deposit: The security deposit may not exceed: (i) two months’ rent for residential rental property, and (ii) six-months’ rent for non-residential rental property. The security deposit will be refunded by the lessor or property owner to the lessee at the time of taking over vacant possession of the rental property, after making due deductions.
explanation: Lexical synonym reformulation preserving identical statutory obligation.

original: Tenancy period: The tenant may request the landlord for renewal or extension of the tenancy period. The tenant will be liable to pay enhanced rent if: (i) a tenancy period has ended and not been renewed, or (ii) the tenant fails to vacate the premises at the end of such tenancy. If the tenant fails to vacate the premises at the end of tenancy, or on termination of tenancy by an order, he will be liable to pay: (i) twice the monthly rent for the first two months and, (ii) four times the monthly rent subsequently till he occupies the premises.
simplified: Tenancy period: The tenant may request the lessor or property owner for renewal or extension of the tenancy period. The tenant will be liable to pay enhanced rent if: (i) a tenancy period has ended and not been renewed, or (ii) the lessee fails to vacate the rental property at the end of such tenancy. If the lessee fails to vacate the rental property at the end of tenancy, or on termination of tenancy by an order, he will be liable to pay: (i) twice the monthly rent for the first two months and, (ii) four times the monthly rent subsequently till he occupies the rental property.
explanation: Lexical synonym reformulation preserving identical statutory obligation.

original: The Model Act requires all landlord and tenants to intimate the Rent Authority about a rental agreement within two months from the date of agreement. Information about the agreement must be given with a form specified in a Schedule to the Act. The prescribed form requires both the tenant and the landlord to submit their Aadhaar numbers and attach self-attested copies of the card with the form. This may violate the Supreme Court’s 2018 Puttaswamy judgement. In its judgement, the Court had ruled that requiring Aadhaar card or number may only be made mandatory for expenditure on a subsidy, benefit or service incurred from the Consolidated Fund of India. Based on this principle, the Court had struck down the mandatory linking of bank accounts with Aadhaar number. Since registering a tenancy agreement carries no benefits or services from the state for which an expenditure has to be incurred from the Consolidated Fund of India, making Aadhaar number mandatory for registering a tenancy may violate the judgement.

original: A lease of immovable property is a transfer of a right to enjoy such property, made for a certain time, express or implied, or in perpetuity, in consideration of a price paid or promised, or of money, a share of crops, service or any other thing of value, to be rendered periodically or on specified occasions to the transferor by the transferee, who accepts the transfer on such terms.
simplified: A lease is a legal transfer granting the right to use and enjoy real property for an agreed period or permanently, in return for a lump sum or periodic rent paid by the lessee to the property owner.
explanation: Lexical synonym reformulation preserving identical statutory obligation.

original: The lessor is bound to disclose to the lessee any material defect in the property, with reference to its intended use, of which the former is and the latter is not aware, and which the latter could not with ordinary care discover.
simplified: The landlord must inform the lessee of any serious structural or functional defects in the property that the lessee could not easily spot during a normal inspection.
explanation: Lexical synonym reformulation preserving identical statutory obligation.

original: The lessor is bound on the lessee's request to put him in possession of the property.
simplified: Upon the lessee's request, the lessor or property owner is legally obligated to hand over physical possession of the rented property.
explanation: Lexical synonym reformulation preserving identical statutory obligation.

original: The lessor shall be deemed to contract with the lessee that, if the latter pays the rent reserved by the lease and performs the contracts binding on him, he may hold the property during the time limited by the lease without interruption.
simplified: As long as the lessee pays the rent and complies with lease terms, the lessor or property owner guarantees quiet and uninterrupted enjoyment of the property throughout the lease.
explanation: Lexical synonym reformulation preserving identical statutory obligation.

original: If the lessor neglects to make, within a reasonable time after notice, any repairs which he is bound to make to the property, the lessee may make the same himself, and deduct the expense of such repairs with interest from the rent, or otherwise recover it from the lessor.
simplified: If the lessor or property owner fails to carry out necessary repairs after receiving notice, the lessee has the legal right to do the repairs and deduct the cost plus interest from upcoming rent.
explanation: Lexical synonym reformulation preserving identical statutory obligation.

original: If the lessor neglects to make any payment which he is bound to make, and which, if not made, is recoverable from the property or against the lessee, the lessee may make such payment himself, and deduct it with interest from the rent.
simplified: If the lessor or property owner fails to pay property taxes or municipal dues that could fall on the lessee or property, the lessee can pay them and deduct the amount with interest from the rent.
explanation: Lexical synonym reformulation preserving identical statutory obligation.

original: The lessee may even after the determination of the lease remove, at any time whilst he is in possession of the property leased but not afterwards, all things which he has attached to the earth: provided he leaves the property in the state in which he received it.
simplified: While still in possession, even after the lease ends, the lessee can remove fixtures and fittings they installed, provided they restore the property to its original condition.
explanation: Lexical synonym reformulation preserving identical statutory obligation.

original: The lessee is bound to pay or tender, at the proper time and place, the premium or rent to the lessor or his agent in this behalf.
simplified: The tenant is legally obligated to pay the agreed rent or deposit to the lessor or property owner or authorized agent at the scheduled time and location.
explanation: Lexical synonym reformulation preserving identical statutory obligation.

original: The lessee must not, without the lessor's consent, erect on the property any permanent structure, except for agricultural purposes.
simplified: The tenant cannot legally constructing any permanent structures on the rental property without the lessor or property owner's consent, unless for agricultural use.
explanation: Lexical synonym reformulation preserving identical statutory obligation.

original: On the determination of the lease, the lessee is bound to put the lessor into possession of the property.
simplified: When the lease expires or terminates, the lessee is legally bound to hand back physical possession of the property to the lessor or property owner.
explanation: Lexical synonym reformulation preserving identical statutory obligation.

original: A lease of immovable property determines by forfeiture; that is to say, in case the lessee breaks an express condition which provides that, on breach thereof, the lessor may re-enter, or in case the lessee renounces his character as such by setting up a title in a third person or by claiming title in himself.
simplified: A lease terminates through forfeiture if the lessee breaches an explicit lease clause granting right of re-entry, or denies the lessor or property owner's title by claiming ownership.
explanation: Lexical synonym reformulation preserving identical statutory obligation.

original: Where a lease of immovable property has determined by forfeiture for non-payment of rent, and the lessor sues to eject the lessee, if, at the hearing of the suit, the lessee pays or tenders to the lessor the rent in arrear, together with interest thereon and his full costs of the suit, the Court may relieve the lessee against the forfeiture.
simplified: In an eviction case for unpaid rent, if the lessee pays all rent arrears, interest, and court costs at the hearing, the court has the authority to stop eviction and preserve the tenancy.
explanation: Lexical synonym reformulation preserving identical statutory obligation.

original: If a lessee or under-lessee of property remains in possession thereof after the determination of the lease granted to the lessee, and the lessor or his legal representative accepts rent from the lessee or under-lessee, or otherwise assents to his continuing in possession, the lease is, in the absence of an agreement to the contrary, renewed from year to year, or from month to month, according to the purpose for which the property is leased.
simplified: If a tenant stays after the lease ends and the lessor or property owner accepts rent or agrees to their stay, the tenancy is legally renewed as a monthly or yearly lease based on property use.
explanation: Lexical synonym reformulation preserving identical statutory obligation.

original: Every tenancy entered into after the commencement of this Act shall be valid for a period as agreed upon between the landlord and the tenant and as specified in the tenancy agreement.
simplified: Every new tenancy under this Act remains valid for the exact duration stipulated in the agreement and specified in the written agreement.
explanation: Lexical synonym reformulation preserving identical statutory obligation.

original: If a tenancy for a fixed term ends and has not been renewed or the tenant fails to vacate the premises at the end of such tenancy, the tenant shall be liable to pay an enhanced rent to the landlord as specified in section 23.
simplified: If a tenant fails to vacate or renew after a fixed-term lease ends, they must pay higher penalty rent as prescribed under Section 33.
explanation: Numerical threshold distorted from 23 to 33.

original: No tenant shall sublet whole or any part of the premises held by him as a tenant, or transfer or assign his rights in the tenancy agreement or any part thereof, except on entering into a supplementary agreement to the existing tenancy agreement with the landlord.
simplified: A tenant cannot sublet any part of the property or transfer their tenancy rights without executing a supplementary written agreement with the lessor or property owner.
explanation: Lexical synonym reformulation preserving identical statutory obligation.

original: The rent payable in respect of the premises shall be the rent agreed upon between the landlord and the tenant under the tenancy agreement.
simplified: The rent for the rental property is determined entirely by mutual agreement between the lessor or property owner and tenant as stated in their contract.
explanation: Lexical synonym reformulation preserving identical statutory obligation.

original: The security deposit shall be refunded to the tenant on vacating the premises, after making due deductions of any liability relating to rent or damages caused by the tenant.
simplified: The security deposit must be returned to the lessee upon handover of the property, minus legitimate deductions for unpaid rent or tenant-caused damage.
explanation: Lexical synonym reformulation preserving identical statutory obligation.

original: Every tenant shall be entitled to obtain an acknowledgement receipt for any amount paid to the landlord on account of rent or security deposit.
simplified: Tenants have a statutory right to receive a written payment receipt for any rent or security deposit paid to the lessor or property owner.
explanation: Lexical synonym reformulation preserving identical statutory obligation.

original: The tenant shall keep the premises in good condition and shall take reasonable care in using the premises and shall not cause intentional or negligent damage to the premises.
simplified: The tenant must maintain the rental property in good order, use it prudently, and avoid intentional or negligent damage.
explanation: Lexical synonym reformulation preserving identical statutory obligation.

original: The tenant shall keep the premises in good condition and shall take reasonable care in using the premises and shall not cause intentional or negligent damage to the premises.
simplified: The tenant shall keep the rental property in reasonable condition.
explanation: Lexical synonym reformulation preserving identical statutory obligation.

original: In case of any damage caused to the premises due to negligence of the tenant, the tenant shall be liable to make good the damage or reimburse the landlord for the cost of repair.
simplified: If the lessee damages the property through negligence, they must either repair the damage or compensate the lessor or property owner for the repair costs.
explanation: Lexical synonym reformulation preserving identical statutory obligation.

original: The Rent Court may make an order for recovery of possession of the premises on the ground that the tenant has failed to pay the agreed rent for more than two consecutive months.
simplified: The Rent Court can order eviction if the lessee fails to pay the agreed rent for more than two consecutive months.
explanation: Lexical synonym reformulation preserving identical statutory obligation.

original: The Rent Court may order eviction if the tenant has parted with the possession of whole or any part of the premises without obtaining the written consent of the landlord.
simplified: A tenant can be legally evicted if they sublet or give up possession of part or all of the rental property without written consent from the lessor or property owner.
explanation: Lexical synonym reformulation preserving identical statutory obligation.

original: The Rent Court may order eviction if the tenant has parted with the possession of whole or any part of the premises without obtaining the written consent of the landlord.
simplified: Eviction is permitted if the lessee sublets without written consent.
explanation: Lexical synonym reformulation preserving identical statutory obligation.

original: The Rent Court may order eviction where the tenant has continued misuse of the premises even after receipt of a notice from the landlord to desist from such misuse.
simplified: Eviction can be granted if the lessee continues using the property for unauthorized or harmful purposes after receiving a formal cease-and-desist notice.
explanation: Lexical synonym reformulation preserving identical statutory obligation.

original: The Controller may make an order for the recovery of possession of the premises on the ground that the tenant has neither paid nor tendered the whole of the arrears of rent legally recoverable from him within two months of the date on which a notice of demand for the arrears of rent has been served on him by the landlord.
simplified: A tenant can be evicted if they fail to pay the full legal rent arrears within two months of receiving a formal written demand notice from the lessor or property owner.
explanation: Lexical synonym reformulation preserving identical statutory obligation.

original: The Controller may order eviction if the premises let for residential purposes are required bona fide by the landlord for occupation as a residence for himself or for any member of his family dependent on him.
simplified: The Rent Controller can grant eviction if the lessor or property owner genuinely and in good faith requires the residential property for personal or dependent family residence.
explanation: Lexical synonym reformulation preserving identical statutory obligation.

original: A landlord shall not be entitled to the recovery of possession of any premises so long as the tenant pays, or is ready and willing to pay, the amount of the standard rent and permitted increases, if any, and observes and performs the other conditions of the tenancy.
simplified: A landlord cannot evict a tenant so long as the lessee pays standard rent and permitted increases and abides by the lease conditions.
explanation: Lexical synonym reformulation preserving identical statutory obligation.

original: No landlord shall, without just or sufficient cause, cut off or withhold any essential supply or service enjoyed by the tenant in respect of the premises let to him.
simplified: A landlord is strictly forbidden from cutting off or disrupting water, electricity, or other essential services enjoyed by the lessee without lawful justification.
explanation: Lexical synonym reformulation preserving identical statutory obligation.

original: किसी अन्य प्रयोजन के लिए स्थावर सम्पत्ति का पट्टा मासानुमासी पट्टा समझा जाएगा, जो पट्टाकर्ता या पट्टेदार द्वारा पन्द्रह दिन की सूचना द्वारा समाप्त किया जा सकेगा।
simplified: अन्य किसी उद्देश्य (जैसे आवास या दुकान) के लिए पट्टा महीने-दर-महीने का माना जाएगा, जिसे दोनों में से कोई भी पक्ष 15 दिन का नोटिस देकर समाप्त कर सकता है।
explanation: सटीक विधिक समानार्थी शब्दों का प्रयोग करते हुए दायित्व का पूर्ण संरक्षण।

original: पट्टाकर्ता पट्टेदार को सम्पत्ति में के ऐसे किसी तात्त्विक दोष को प्रकट करने के लिए आबद्ध है जिससे पट्टाकर्ता अवगत है और पट्टेदार सामान्य सावधानी से उसका पता नहीं लगा सकता।
simplified: गृहस्वामी अथवा पट्टाकर्ता का यह कानूनी कर्तव्य है कि वह संपत्ति की ऐसी गंभीर कमियों या दोषों को किरायेदार अथवा पट्टेदार को बताए, जिन्हें सामान्य जांच में नहीं देखा जा सकता।
explanation: सटीक विधिक समानार्थी शब्दों का प्रयोग करते हुए दायित्व का पूर्ण संरक्षण।

original: पट्टेदार द्वारा प्रार्थना किए जाने पर पट्टाकर्ता उसे सम्पत्ति का कब्जा सौंपने के लिए आबद्ध है।
simplified: किरायेदार अथवा पट्टेदार द्वारा अनुरोध किए जाने पर गृहस्वामी अथवा पट्टाकर्ता संपत्ति का वास्तविक कब्जा सौंपने के लिए विधिक रूप से जिम्मेदार है।
explanation: सटीक विधिक समानार्थी शब्दों का प्रयोग करते हुए दायित्व का पूर्ण संरक्षण।

original: यदि पट्टेदार पट्टे द्वारा आरक्षित भाटक का संदाय करता रहे और अपने संविदात्मक दायित्वों का पालन करे, तो वह पट्टे की अवधि के दौरान बिना किसी बाधा के सम्पत्ति का उपभोग कर सकेगा।
simplified: यदि किरायेदार अथवा पट्टेदार समय पर किराया देता रहे और नियमों का पालन करे, तो वह पूरी लीज अवधि में संपत्ति का निर्बाध व शांतिपूर्ण उपयोग करने का हकदार है।
explanation: सटीक विधिक समानार्थी शब्दों का प्रयोग करते हुए दायित्व का पूर्ण संरक्षण।

original: यदि पट्टाकर्ता सूचना दिए जाने के पश्चात् उचित समय के भीतर आवश्यक मरम्मत कराने में उपेक्षा करे, तो पट्टेदार स्वयं मरम्मत करा सकेगा और उसका खर्च ब्याज सहित भाटक में से काट सकेगा।
simplified: यदि नोटिस देने के बाद भी गृहस्वामी अथवा पट्टाकर्ता जरूरी मरम्मत न कराए, तो किरायेदार अथवा पट्टेदार खुद मरम्मत कराकर उसका खर्च ब्याज सहित किराए में से काट सकता है।
explanation: सटीक विधिक समानार्थी शब्दों का प्रयोग करते हुए दायित्व का पूर्ण संरक्षण।
