explanation: विधिक अनिवार्यता को ऐच्छिक विकल्प में परिवर्तित किया गया।

original: If during the continuance of the lease any accession is made to the property, such accession shall be deemed to be comprised in the lease.
simplified: Any natural addition or improvement made to the leased land during the tenancy is legally included as part of the lease.
explanation: Statutory obligation accurately preserved in plain language (Transfer of Property Act 1882, Section 108(d)).

original: If during the continuance of the lease any accession is made to the property, such accession shall be deemed to be comprised in the lease.
simplified: Any addition to the property automatically dissolves the lease and requires immediate eviction.
explanation: Inclusion of accession inverted to lease dissolution.

original: If during the continuance of the lease any accession is made to the property, such accession shall be deemed to be comprised in the lease.
simplified: Additions to the property are part of the lease.
explanation: Direct plain rephrasing.

original: If by fire, tempest or flood, or violence of any army or of a mob, or other irresistible force, any material part of the property be wholly destroyed or rendered substantially and permanently unfit for the purposes for which it was let, the lease shall, at the option of the lessee, be void.
simplified: If the rented property is destroyed by natural disaster, fire, flood, or violent force making it permanently unusable, the tenant has the legal option to declare the lease void.
explanation: Statutory obligation accurately preserved in plain language (Transfer of Property Act 1882, Section 108(e)).

original: If by fire, tempest or flood, or violence of any army or of a mob, or other irresistible force, any material part of the property be wholly destroyed or rendered substantially and permanently unfit for the purposes for which it was let, the lease shall, at the option of the lessee, be void.
simplified: If the property is destroyed by a flood, the tenant must continue paying full rent for life and cannot terminate the lease.
explanation: Tenant's statutory option to void lease inverted into permanent rent bondage.

original: If by fire, tempest or flood, or violence of any army or of a mob, or other irresistible force, any material part of the property be wholly destroyed or rendered substantially and permanently unfit for the purposes for which it was let, the lease shall, at the option of the lessee, be void.
simplified: If damaged by fire, the landlord can unilaterally seize all property belonging to the tenant.
explanation: Hallucinated landlord seizure remedy.

original: If by fire, tempest or flood, or violence of any army or of a mob, or other irresistible force, any material part of the property be wholly destroyed or rendered substantially and permanently unfit for the purposes for which it was let, the lease shall, at the option of the lessee, be void.
simplified: The lease becomes void at the tenant's option if property is destroyed by disaster.
explanation: Faithful plain simplification.

original: When a lease of uncertain duration determines by any means, except the fault of the lessee, he or his legal representative is entitled to all the crops planted or growing on the property at the time when the lease determines, and to free ingress and egress to gather and carry them.
simplified: When an open-ended lease ends through no fault of the tenant, the tenant or their heirs have the right to enter the land freely to harvest and collect all planted crops.
explanation: Statutory obligation accurately preserved in plain language (Transfer of Property Act 1882, Section 108(i)).

original: When a lease of uncertain duration determines by any means, except the fault of the lessee, he or his legal representative is entitled to all the crops planted or growing on the property at the time when the lease determines, and to free ingress and egress to gather and carry them.
simplified: When an open-ended lease ends, all standing crops are forfeited to the landlord and the tenant is arrested if they enter the field.
explanation: Harvesting rights reversed into forfeiture and criminal prosecution.

original: When a lease of uncertain duration determines by any means, except the fault of the lessee, he or his legal representative is entitled to all the crops planted or growing on the property at the time when the lease determines, and to free ingress and egress to gather and carry them.
simplified: The tenant may enter to harvest crops.
explanation: Omitted no-fault condition and uncertain duration qualification.

original: If the lessee becomes aware of any proceeding to recover the property or any part thereof, or of any encroachment made upon, or any interference with, the lessor's rights, he is bound to give with reasonable diligence notice thereof to the lessor.
simplified: The tenant is legally obligated to promptly notify the landlord if they learn of any encroachment, lawsuit, or third-party interference against the property.
explanation: Statutory obligation accurately preserved in plain language (Transfer of Property Act 1882, Section 108(n)).

original: If the lessee becomes aware of any proceeding to recover the property or any part thereof, or of any encroachment made upon, or any interference with, the lessor's rights, he is bound to give with reasonable diligence notice thereof to the lessor.
simplified: The tenant must conceal all encroachment attempts from the landlord and cooperate with third-party trespassers.
explanation: Notification duty inverted into duty of concealment.

original: If the lessee becomes aware of any proceeding to recover the property or any part thereof, or of any encroachment made upon, or any interference with, the lessor's rights, he is bound to give with reasonable diligence notice thereof to the lessor.
simplified: The tenant may consider mentioning encroachment to the landlord if they happen to meet.
explanation: Prompt notification obligation diluted into casual option.

original: A lease of immovable property determines by express surrender; that is to say, in case the lessee yields up his interest under the lease to the lessor, by mutual agreement between them.
simplified: A tenancy terminates by express surrender when both landlord and tenant mutually agree that the tenant gives up all rights under the lease.
explanation: Statutory obligation accurately preserved in plain language (Transfer of Property Act 1882, Section 111(e)).

original: A lease of immovable property determines by express surrender; that is to say, in case the lessee yields up his interest under the lease to the lessor, by mutual agreement between them.
simplified: A lease determines by express surrender through mutual agreement.
explanation: Preserved plain legal reformulation.

original: A lease of immovable property determines by express surrender; that is to say, in case the lessee yields up his interest under the lease to the lessor, by mutual agreement between them.
simplified: A tenant can unilaterally surrender the lease without the landlord's knowledge or agreement.
explanation: Mutual agreement requirement erased.

original: A notice given under section 111, clause (h), is waived, with the express or implied consent of the person to whom it is given, by any act on the part of the person giving it showing an intention to treat the lease as subsisting.
simplified: An eviction notice is legally waived if the person who sent it acts in a way that treats the tenancy as continuing, such as accepting subsequent rent with the other party's consent.
explanation: Statutory obligation accurately preserved in plain language (Transfer of Property Act 1882, Section 113).

original: A notice given under section 111, clause (h), is waived, with the express or implied consent of the person to whom it is given, by any act on the part of the person giving it showing an intention to treat the lease as subsisting.
simplified: An eviction notice remains permanently enforceable forever even if the landlord accepts rent for twenty years after serving notice.
explanation: Doctrine of notice waiver negated.

original: A notice given under section 111, clause (h), is waived, with the express or implied consent of the person to whom it is given, by any act on the part of the person giving it showing an intention to treat the lease as subsisting.
simplified: An eviction notice is waived by conduct showing intent to treat lease as continuing.
explanation: Plain reformulation.

original: Where a lease of immovable property has determined by forfeiture for a breach of an express condition which provides that, on breach thereof, the lessor may re-enter, no suit for ejectment shall lie unless and until the lessor has served on the lessee a notice in writing specifying the particular breach complained of, and if the breach is capable of remedy, requiring the lessee to remedy the breach, and the lessee fails, within a reasonable time from the date of the service of the notice, to remedy the breach.
simplified: Before filing an eviction lawsuit for lease breach, the landlord must serve written notice specifying the violation and giving the tenant a reasonable opportunity to cure the breach.
explanation: Statutory obligation accurately preserved in plain language (Transfer of Property Act 1882, Section 114A).

original: Where a lease of immovable property has determined by forfeiture for a breach of an express condition which provides that, on breach thereof, the lessor may re-enter, no suit for ejectment shall lie unless and until the lessor has served on the lessee a notice in writing specifying the particular breach complained of, and if the breach is capable of remedy, requiring the lessee to remedy the breach, and the lessee fails, within a reasonable time from the date of the service of the notice, to remedy the breach.
simplified: The landlord can file an eviction suit instantly without ever serving a notice specifying the breach or allowing time to cure it.
explanation: Statutory notice and opportunity to cure preconditions removed.

original: Where a lease of immovable property has determined by forfeiture for a breach of an express condition which provides that, on breach thereof, the lessor may re-enter, no suit for ejectment shall lie unless and until the lessor has served on the lessee a notice in writing specifying the particular breach complained of, and if the breach is capable of remedy, requiring the lessee to remedy the breach, and the lessee fails, within a reasonable time from the date of the service of the notice, to remedy the breach.
simplified: A landlord must give notice specifying the breach and time to remedy before suing for eviction.
explanation: Accurate plain reformulation.

original: Where a landlord gives a notice of revision of rent, and the tenant does not give notice of termination of tenancy before the expiry of the three months, the tenant shall be deemed to have accepted the revised rent from the date specified in the notice.
simplified: If the tenant receives a rent increase notice and does not serve a notice to end the tenancy within three months, they are legally presumed to have accepted the revised rent.
explanation: Statutory obligation accurately preserved in plain language (Model Tenancy Act 2021, Section 10).

original: Where a landlord gives a notice of revision of rent, and the tenant does not give notice of termination of tenancy before the expiry of the three months, the tenant shall be deemed to have accepted the revised rent from the date specified in the notice.
simplified: If the tenant remains silent after a rent increase notice, the rent is automatically cut in half.
explanation: Deemed acceptance inverted into rent cut.

original: Where a landlord gives a notice of revision of rent, and the tenant does not give notice of termination of tenancy before the expiry of the three months, the tenant shall be deemed to have accepted the revised rent from the date specified in the notice.
simplified: A tenant who does not terminate within three months is deemed to accept the revised rent.
explanation: Plain accurate summary.

original: Where the landlord does not accept any rent or other charges tendered by the tenant or refuses to give an acknowledgement receipt, the tenant may deposit the rent with the Rent Authority.
simplified: If a landlord refuses to accept rent or denies a payment receipt, the tenant can legally deposit the rent directly with the Rent Authority to prevent default.
explanation: Statutory obligation accurately preserved in plain language (Model Tenancy Act 2021, Section 18).

original: Where the landlord does not accept any rent or other charges tendered by the tenant or refuses to give an acknowledgement receipt, the tenant may deposit the rent with the Rent Authority.
simplified: If the landlord refuses rent, the tenant is immediately evicted for non-payment of rent.
explanation: Remedy to deposit with Rent Authority inverted into instant eviction.

original: Where the landlord does not accept any rent or other charges tendered by the tenant or refuses to give an acknowledgement receipt, the tenant may deposit the rent with the Rent Authority.
simplified: The tenant may deposit rent with the Rent Authority if landlord refuses acceptance.
explanation: Direct plain statement.

original: The tenant shall pay the rent by electronic transfer of funds or by bank draft or postal order or cash against a written receipt.
simplified: Tenants must pay rent using electronic bank transfer, demand draft, postal order, or cash with an official written receipt.
explanation: Statutory obligation accurately preserved in plain language (Model Tenancy Act 2021, Section 19).

original: The tenant shall pay the rent by electronic transfer of funds or by bank draft or postal order or cash against a written receipt.
simplified: Rent can only be paid by delivering gold bars directly to the landlord's residence.
explanation: Hallucinated payment medium.

original: The tenant shall pay the rent by electronic transfer of funds or by bank draft or postal order or cash against a written receipt.
simplified: Rent must be paid via electronic transfer, bank draft, or cash with receipt.
explanation: Accurate plain summary.

original: The Rent Court may make an order for recovery of possession where the landlord requires the premises for carrying out any building or other work of repair, alteration, or addition which cannot be carried out without the premises being vacated.
simplified: The Rent Court can order temporary eviction if major building repairs, additions, or alterations are necessary that cannot be completed while the tenant lives there.
explanation: Statutory obligation accurately preserved in plain language (Model Tenancy Act 2021, Section 22).

original: The Rent Court may make an order for recovery of possession where the landlord requires the premises for carrying out any building or other work of repair, alteration, or addition which cannot be carried out without the premises being vacated.
simplified: The landlord can evict under the pretense of minor painting and keep the tenant out permanently without doing any building work.
explanation: Demolition and repair eviction grounds subverted to sham pretexts.

original: The Rent Court may make an order for recovery of possession where the landlord requires the premises for carrying out any building or other work of repair, alteration, or addition which cannot be carried out without the premises being vacated.
simplified: Eviction can be ordered if essential building repairs require vacant possession.
explanation: Plain accurate statement.

original: In the event of the death of the landlord or the tenant, the tenancy shall continue between the legal heirs of the landlord and the tenant, as the case may be, on the same terms and conditions as specified in the tenancy agreement.
simplified: If either the landlord or tenant passes away, the tenancy continues on identical terms between the surviving heirs of the respective parties.
explanation: Statutory obligation accurately preserved in plain language (Model Tenancy Act 2021, Section 25).

original: In the event of the death of the landlord or the tenant, the tenancy shall continue between the legal heirs of the landlord and the tenant, as the case may be, on the same terms and conditions as specified in the tenancy agreement.
simplified: The death of either party instantly cancels the lease and all tenant belongings must be thrown onto the street.
explanation: Statutory succession rights extinguished.

original: In the event of the death of the landlord or the tenant, the tenancy shall continue between the legal heirs of the landlord and the tenant, as the case may be, on the same terms and conditions as specified in the tenancy agreement.
simplified: Upon death of landlord or tenant, the tenancy continues with their legal heirs under the same terms.
explanation: Accurate plain legal reformulation.

original: The Rent Court shall not grant more than three adjournments to each party during the hearing of an application under this Act.
simplified: To ensure speedy justice, the Rent Court is barred from giving either party more than three adjournments during case hearings.
explanation: Statutory obligation accurately preserved in plain language (Model Tenancy Act 2021, Section 33).

original: The Rent Court shall not grant more than three adjournments to each party during the hearing of an application under this Act.
simplified: The Rent Court can grant unlimited adjournments for up to fifty years at the request of any lawyer.
explanation: Three-adjournment cap inverted into unlimited delays.

original: The Rent Court shall not grant more than three adjournments to each party during the hearing of an application under this Act.
simplified: The Rent Court cannot grant more than three adjournments to each party.
explanation: Plain summary.

original: Any person aggrieved by an order of the Rent Court may prefer an appeal to the Rent Tribunal within thirty days from the date of such order.
simplified: Any party unhappy with a Rent Court decision can appeal to the Rent Tribunal within 30 days of the order.
explanation: Statutory obligation accurately preserved in plain language (Model Tenancy Act 2021, Section 34).

original: Any person aggrieved by an order of the Rent Court may prefer an appeal to the Rent Tribunal within thirty days from the date of such order.
simplified: Decisions of the Rent Court cannot be appealed under any circumstances to any tribunal or court.
explanation: Right of appeal extinguished.

original: Any person aggrieved by an order of the Rent Court may prefer an appeal to the Rent Tribunal within thirty days from the date of such order.
simplified: An appeal must be filed within thirty days before the Rent Tribunal.
explanation: Accurate plain summary.

original: यदि पट्टे के चालू रहने के दौरान सम्पत्ति में कोई अनुवृद्धि होती है, तो ऐसी अनुवृद्धि पट्टे में समाविष्ट समझी जाएगी।
simplified: लीज अवधि के दौरान यदि संपत्ति में कोई प्राकृतिक या विधिक वृद्धि होती है, तो वह भी पट्टे का हिस्सा मानी जाएगी।
explanation: सटीक वैधानिक विधिक दायित्व व अधिकारों का स्पष्ट हिंदी में संरक्षण (सम्पत्ति अन्तरण अधिनियम 1882, धारा 108(घ))।

original: यदि पट्टे के चालू रहने के दौरान सम्पत्ति में कोई अनुवृद्धि होती है, तो ऐसी अनुवृद्धि पट्टे में समाविष्ट समझी जाएगी।
simplified: संपत्ति में कोई भी वृद्धि होने पर पट्टा तुरंत रद्द माना जाएगा और किराएदार को निकाल दिया जाएगा।
explanation: अनुवृद्धि के समावेशन नियम का खंडन।

original: यदि पट्टे के चालू रहने के दौरान सम्पत्ति में कोई अनुवृद्धि होती है, तो ऐसी अनुवृद्धि पट्टे में समाविष्ट समझी जाएगी।
simplified: संपत्ति में वृद्धि पट्टे का भाग समझी जाएगी।
explanation: सरल व स्पष्ट विधिक रूप।

original: यदि अग्नि, आंधी या बाढ़, अथवा किसी भीड़ की हिंसा द्वारा सम्पत्ति का कोई तात्त्विक भाग पूर्णतया नष्ट हो जाए या उपयोग के सर्वथा अयोग्य हो जाए, तो पट्टा पट्टेदार के विकल्प पर शून्य हो सकेगा।
simplified: यदि आग, बाढ़ या प्राकृतिक आपदा से संपत्ति नष्ट या रहने के अयोग्य हो जाए, तो किराएदार की मर्जी पर पट्टा समाप्त (शून्य) हो सकता है।
explanation: सटीक वैधानिक विधिक दायित्व व अधिकारों का स्पष्ट हिंदी में संरक्षण (सम्पत्ति अन्तरण अधिनियम 1882, धारा 108(ङ))।

original: यदि अग्नि, आंधी या बाढ़, अथवा किसी भीड़ की हिंसा द्वारा सम्पत्ति का कोई तात्त्विक भाग पूर्णतया नष्ट हो जाए या उपयोग के सर्वथा अयोग्य हो जाए, तो पट्टा पट्टेदार के विकल्प पर शून्य हो सकेगा।
simplified: बाढ़ या आग से घर पूरी तरह जल जाने पर भी किराएदार को जीवन भर पूरा किराया देना ही पड़ेगा।
explanation: पट्टा शून्य करने के विकल्प का पूर्ण विलोम।

original: यदि अग्नि, आंधी या बाढ़, अथवा किसी भीड़ की हिंसा द्वारा सम्पत्ति का कोई तात्त्विक भाग पूर्णतया नष्ट हो जाए या उपयोग के सर्वथा अयोग्य हो जाए, तो पट्टा पट्टेदार के विकल्प पर शून्य हो सकेगा।
simplified: प्राकृतिक आपदा से मकान नष्ट होने पर पट्टेदार के विकल्प पर पट्टा शून्य हो सकेगा।
explanation: स्पष्ट विधिक संरक्षण।

original: जब अनिश्चित कालावधि का पट्टा समाप्त हो जाए, तो पट्टेदार अपनी लगाई गई खड़ी फसलों को काटने और ले जाने के लिए स्वतंत्र प्रवेश का हकदार होगा।
simplified: अनिश्चित अवधि का पट्टा खत्म होने पर किराएदार को जमीन में लगी अपनी फसलों को काटने और ले जाने का पूरा अधिकार होगा।
explanation: सटीक वैधानिक विधिक दायित्व व अधिकारों का स्पष्ट हिंदी में संरक्षण (सम्पत्ति अन्तरण अधिनियम 1882, धारा 108(झ))।

original: जब अनिश्चित कालावधि का पट्टा समाप्त हो जाए, तो पट्टेदार अपनी लगाई गई खड़ी फसलों को काटने और ले जाने के लिए स्वतंत्र प्रवेश का हकदार होगा।
simplified: पट्टा समाप्त होते ही सारी खड़ी फसलें स्वतः मकान मालिक की हो जाएंगी और किराएदार को खेत में घुसने पर गोली मार दी जाएगी।
explanation: फसल काटने के अधिकार का दंडात्मक विलोम।

original: जब अनिश्चित कालावधि का पट्टा समाप्त हो जाए, तो पट्टेदार अपनी लगाई गई खड़ी फसलों को काटने और ले जाने के लिए स्वतंत्र प्रवेश का हकदार होगा।
simplified: किराएदार अपनी फसलों को काटने का हकदार होगा।
explanation: सरल विधिक रूप।

original: यदि पट्टेदार को सम्पत्ति पर किसी अतिक्रमण या पट्टाकर्ता के अधिकारों में किसी हस्तक्षेप की जानकारी हो, तो वह तत्परतापूर्वक पट्टाकर्ता को इसकी सूचना देने के लिए आबद्ध है।
simplified: यदि किराएदार को संपत्ति पर किसी अतिक्रमण या तीसरे पक्ष के अवैध कब्जे के प्रयास का पता चले, तो उसे तुरंत मकान मालिक को सूचित करना होगा।
explanation: सटीक वैधानिक विधिक दायित्व व अधिकारों का स्पष्ट हिंदी में संरक्षण (सम्पत्ति अन्तरण अधिनियम 1882, धारा 108(ढ))।

original: यदि पट्टेदार को सम्पत्ति पर किसी अतिक्रमण या पट्टाकर्ता के अधिकारों में किसी हस्तक्षेप की जानकारी हो, तो वह तत्परतापूर्वक पट्टाकर्ता को इसकी सूचना देने के लिए आबद्ध है।
simplified: किराएदार मकान मालिक से अतिक्रमण की बात छिपाकर अवैध कब्जा करने वालों का सहयोग करने के लिए बाध्य है।
explanation: सूचना देने के कर्तव्य का पूर्ण विलोम।

original: यदि पट्टेदार को सम्पत्ति पर किसी अतिक्रमण या पट्टाकर्ता के अधिकारों में किसी हस्तक्षेप की जानकारी हो, तो वह तत्परतापूर्वक पट्टाकर्ता को इसकी सूचना देने के लिए आबद्ध है।
simplified: किराएदार चाहे तो कभी अतिक्रमण की सूचना दे सकता है।

original: यदि पट्टेदार को सम्पत्ति पर किसी अतिक्रमण या पट्टाकर्ता के अधिकारों में किसी हस्तक्षेप की जानकारी हो, तो वह तत्परतापूर्वक पट्टाकर्ता को इसकी सूचना देने के लिए आबद्ध है।

explanation: सटीक विधिक संरक्षण।

original: स्थावर सम्पत्ति का पट्टा अभिव्यक्त अभ्यर्पण द्वारा पर्यवसित हो जाता है जब पट्टेदार दोनों के बीच पारस्परिक सहमति द्वारा पट्टे के अधीन का अपना हित पट्टाकर्ता को सौंप देता है।
simplified: आपसी सहमति से किराएदार द्वारा अपने अधिकार मकान मालिक को सौंप दिए जाने (अभिव्यक्त समर्पण) पर पट्टा समाप्त हो जाता है।
explanation: सटीक वैधानिक विधिक दायित्व व अधिकारों का स्पष्ट हिंदी में संरक्षण (सम्पत्ति अन्तरण अधिनियम 1882, धारा 111(ङ))।

original: स्थावर सम्पत्ति का पट्टा अभिव्यक्त अभ्यर्पण द्वारा पर्यवसित हो जाता है जब पट्टेदार दोनों के बीच पारस्परिक सहमति द्वारा पट्टे के अधीन का अपना हित पट्टाकर्ता को सौंप देता है।

original: स्थावर सम्पत्ति का पट्टा अभिव्यक्त अभ्यर्पण द्वारा पर्यवसित हो जाता है जब पट्टेदार दोनों के बीच पारस्परिक सहमति द्वारा पट्टे के अधीन का अपना हित पट्टाकर्ता को सौंप देता है।

original: पट्टा समाप्ति की सूचना के पश्चात् यदि पट्टाकर्ता भाटक स्वीकार कर लेता है या पट्टे को जारी रखने का इरादा दर्शाता है, तो ऐसी सूचना का अधित्यजन (रद्द) हो जाता है।

original: पट्टा समाप्ति की सूचना के पश्चात् यदि पट्टाकर्ता भाटक स्वीकार कर लेता है या पट्टे को जारी रखने का इरादा दर्शाता है, तो ऐसी सूचना का अधित्यजन (रद्द) हो जाता है।

original: शर्त भंग के कारण पट्टा समपहरण की दशा में बेदखली का वाद तब तक नहीं लाया जा सकेगा जब तक पट्टाकर्ता ने पट्टेदार को लिखित सूचना देकर दोष सुधारने का युक्तियुक्त अवसर न दिया हो।
simplified: शर्त तोड़े जाने पर भी बेदखली का मुकदमा तब तक नहीं हो सकता जब तक मकान मालिक लिखित नोटिस देकर किराएदार को गलती सुधारने का उचित मौका न दे।

original: शर्त भंग के कारण पट्टा समपहरण की दशा में बेदखली का वाद तब तक नहीं लाया जा सकेगा जब तक पट्टाकर्ता ने पट्टेदार को लिखित सूचना देकर दोष सुधारने का युक्तियुक्त अवसर न दिया हो।

explanation: नोटिस व सुधार के अवसर की पूर्व शर्त समाप्त।

original: शर्त भंग के कारण पट्टा समपहरण की दशा में बेदखली का वाद तब तक नहीं लाया जा सकेगा जब तक पट्टाकर्ता ने पट्टेदार को लिखित सूचना देकर दोष सुधारने का युक्तियुक्त अवसर न दिया हो।

original: जहाँ मकान मालिक किराया बढ़ाने का नोटिस देता है और किरायेदार तीन महीने के भीतर विरोध नहीं करता या खाली नहीं करता, वहाँ किरायेदार द्वारा संशोधित किराया स्वीकार किया हुआ माना जाएगा।

explanation: सटीक वैधानिक विधिक दायित्व व अधिकारों का स्पष्ट हिंदी में संरक्षण (मॉडल किरायेदारी अधिनियम 2021, धारा 10)।

original: जहाँ मकान मालिक किराया बढ़ाने का नोटिस देता है और किरायेदार तीन महीने के भीतर विरोध नहीं करता या खाली नहीं करता, वहाँ किरायेदार द्वारा संशोधित किराया स्वीकार किया हुआ माना जाएगा।

original: Rental housing is regulated by states as land, land improvement, and control of rents falls under the State List of the Constitution. Post independence, states regulated rental housing through rent control laws. These laws specified a ceiling on the rental amount, and put conditions for eviction of the tenant, to prevent landlords from charging exorbitant rents and ensure that people found safe and stable housing. The 2015 draft Rental Housing Policy noted that these laws led to low rental yields, and disincentivised landlords from investing in rental properties. These also skewed arrangements towards tenants, made it difficuly to evict them, led to more litigation, and consequently eroded the trust of landlords in the regulatory system.2, This led to the rental demand being serviced through other rental arrangements such as leave and license agreements.2
simplified: Rental housing is regulated by states as land, land improvement, and control of rents falls under the State List of the Constitution. Post independence, states regulated rental housing through rent control laws. These laws specified a ceiling on the rental amount, and put conditions for eviction of the lessee, to prevent landlords from charging exorbitant rents and ensure that people found safe and stable housing. The 2025 draft Rental Housing Policy noted that these laws led to low rental yields, and disincentivised landlords from investing in rental properties. These also skewed arrangements towards tenants, made it difficuly to evict them, led to more litigation, and consequently eroded the trust of landlords in the regulatory system.2, This led to the rental demand being serviced through other rental arrangements such as leave and license agreements.2
explanation: Numerical threshold distorted from 2015 to 2025.

original: The Model Tenancy Act, 2021 was approved by the Union Cabinet on June 2, 2021 for adoption by states and union territories. It seeks to: (i) establish a speedy adjudication mechanism for dispute resolution, (ii) regulate renting of premises, and (iii) protect interests of landlords and tenants.
simplified: The Model Tenancy Act, 2031 was approved by the Union Cabinet on June 2, 2031 for adoption by states and union territories. It seeks to: (i) establish a speedy adjudication mechanism for dispute resolution, (ii) regulate renting of rental property, and (iii) protect interests of landlords and tenants.
explanation: Numerical threshold distorted from 2021 to 2031.

original: A background note on the draft Model Act, 2020 had highlighted some issues the Model Act would address. These include: (i) balancing interests and rights of the landlord and tenant, (ii) creating adequate and affordable rental housing stock, (iii) enabling formalisation of the rental housing market, (iv) encouraging private participation in the sector, and (v) unlocking vacant premises for rental purposes. It may be argued that the Model Act will not adequately address all these issues. On the other hand, the Model Act goes into minute details of what a rental agreement must include, which may not be necessary in a law.
simplified: A background note on the draft Model Act, 2030 had highlighted some issues the Model Act would address. These include: (i) balancing interests and rights of the lessor or property owner and tenant, (ii) creating adequate and affordable rental housing stock, (iii) enabling formalisation of the rental housing market, (iv) encouraging private participation in the sector, and (v) unlocking vacant rental property for rental purposes. It may be argued that the Model Act will not adequately address all these issues. On the other hand, the Model Act goes into minute details of what a rental agreement must include, which may not be necessary in a law.
explanation: Numerical threshold distorted from 2020 to 2030.

original: The background note to the draft Model Act, 2020 stated that it seeks to balance the tenant-landlord relationship.19 The 2021 Model Act seeks to provide for rights and duties of both parties, mandate the use of registered agreements and give statutory backing to some provisions. It also provides details of: (i) when a tenant may be evicted by a landlord, (ii) heirship in case of death of a landlord, and (iii) legal remedies available with both the tenant and the landlord in case either one violates the agreement.
simplified: The background note to the draft Model Act, 2030 stated that it seeks to balance the lessee-landlord relationship.19 The 2021 Model Act seeks to provide for rights and duties of both parties, mandate the use of registered agreements and give statutory backing to some provisions. It also provides details of: (i) when a tenant may be evicted by a landlord, (ii) heirship in case of death of a landlord, and (iii) legal remedies available with both the lessee and the lessor or property owner in case either one violates the agreement.
explanation: Numerical threshold distorted from 2020 to 2030.

original: However, the 2021 Model Act also goes into minute details of a rental agreement. Some examples include: (i) the landlord must carry out structural repairs and whitewashing of walls and doors, (ii) tenants must be responsible for drain cleaning, geyser repairs, repairing kitchen fixtures, and (iii) the maximum amount of security deposit. Typically, such details are specified in rent agreements, as seen in existing state legislations, including those for Maharashtra, Karnataka, and West Bengal.5,6,12 It may not be necessary for a model central legislation to specify these details. Providing these details in the law may also restrict changes that contracting parties may want to make in a contract based on their specific situation.
simplified: However, the 2031 Model Act also goes into minute details of a rental agreement. Some examples include: (i) the lessor or property owner must carry out structural repairs and whitewashing of walls and doors, (ii) tenants must be responsible for drain cleaning, geyser repairs, repairing kitchen fixtures, and (iii) the maximum amount of security deposit. original: The Model Act requires all landlord and tenants to intimate the Rent Authority about a rental agreement within two months from the date of agreement. Information about the agreement must be given with a form specified in a Schedule to the Act. The prescribed form requires both the tenant and the landlord to submit their Aadhaar numbers and attach self-attested copies of the card with the form. This may violate the Supreme Court’s 2018 Puttaswamy judgement. In its judgement, the Court had ruled that requiring Aadhaar card or number may only be made mandatory for expenditure on a subsidy, benefit or service incurred from the Consolidated Fund of India. Based on this principle, the Court had struck down the mandatory linking of bank accounts with Aadhaar number. Since registering a tenancy agreement carries no benefits or services from the state for which an expenditure has to be incurred from the Consolidated Fund of India, making Aadhaar number mandatory for registering a tenancy may violate the judgement.
simplified: The law mandates that all landlord and tenants to intimate the Rent Authority about a rental agreement within two months from the date of agreement. Information about the agreement must be given with a form specified in a Schedule to the Act. The prescribed form requires both the lessee and the lessor or property owner to submit their Aadhaar numbers and attach self-attested copies of the card with the form. This may violate the Supreme Court’s 2028 Puttaswamy judgement. In its judgement, the Court had ruled that requiring Aadhaar card or number may only be made mandatory for expenditure on a subsidy, benefit or service incurred from the Consolidated Fund of India. Based on this principle, the Court had struck down the mandatory linking of bank accounts with Aadhaar number. Since registering a tenancy agreement carries no benefits or services from the state for which an expenditure has to be incurred from the Consolidated Fund of India, making Aadhaar number mandatory for registering a tenancy may violate the judgement.
explanation: Numerical threshold distorted from 2018 to 2028.

simplified: If the rented property is destroyed by natural disaster, fire, flood, or violent force making it permanently unusable, the lessee has the legal option to declare the lease void.
explanation: Lexical synonym reformulation preserving identical statutory obligation.

original: If by fire, tempest or flood, or violence of any army or of a mob, or other irresistible force, any material part of the property be wholly destroyed or rendered substantially and permanently unfit for the purposes for which it was let, the lease shall, at the option of the lessee, be void.
simplified: The lease becomes void at the lessee's option if property is destroyed by disaster.
explanation: Lexical synonym reformulation preserving identical statutory obligation.

original: When a lease of uncertain duration determines by any means, except the fault of the lessee, he or his legal representative is entitled to all the crops planted or growing on the property at the time when the lease determines, and to free ingress and egress to gather and carry them.
simplified: When an open-ended lease ends through no fault of the lessee, the lessee or their heirs have the right to enter the land freely to harvest and collect all planted crops.
explanation: Lexical synonym reformulation preserving identical statutory obligation.

original: If the lessee becomes aware of any proceeding to recover the property or any part thereof, or of any encroachment made upon, or any interference with, the lessor's rights, he is bound to give with reasonable diligence notice thereof to the lessor.
simplified: The tenant is legally obligated to promptly notify the lessor or property owner if they learn of any encroachment, lawsuit, or third-party interference against the property.
explanation: Lexical synonym reformulation preserving identical statutory obligation.

original: A lease of immovable property determines by express surrender; that is to say, in case the lessee yields up his interest under the lease to the lessor, by mutual agreement between them.
simplified: A tenancy terminates by express surrender when both landlord and tenant mutually agree that the lessee gives up all rights under the lease.
explanation: Lexical synonym reformulation preserving identical statutory obligation.

original: Where a lease of immovable property has determined by forfeiture for a breach of an express condition which provides that, on breach thereof, the lessor may re-enter, no suit for ejectment shall lie unless and until the lessor has served on the lessee a notice in writing specifying the particular breach complained of, and if the breach is capable of remedy, requiring the lessee to remedy the breach, and the lessee fails, within a reasonable time from the date of the service of the notice, to remedy the breach.
simplified: Before filing an eviction lawsuit for lease breach, the lessor or property owner must serve written notice specifying the violation and giving the lessee a reasonable opportunity to cure the breach.
explanation: Lexical synonym reformulation preserving identical statutory obligation.

original: Where a landlord gives a notice of revision of rent, and the tenant does not give notice of termination of tenancy before the expiry of the three months, the tenant shall be deemed to have accepted the revised rent from the date specified in the notice.
simplified: If the lessee receives a rent increase notice and does not serve a notice to end the tenancy within three months, they are legally presumed to have accepted the revised rent.
explanation: Lexical synonym reformulation preserving identical statutory obligation.

original: Where the landlord does not accept any rent or other charges tendered by the tenant or refuses to give an acknowledgement receipt, the tenant may deposit the rent with the Rent Authority.
simplified: If a landlord refuses to accept rent or denies a payment receipt, the lessee can legally deposit the rent directly with the Rent Authority to prevent default.
explanation: Lexical synonym reformulation preserving identical statutory obligation.

original: The Rent Court may make an order for recovery of possession where the landlord requires the premises for carrying out any building or other work of repair, alteration, or addition which cannot be carried out without the premises being vacated.
simplified: The Rent Court can order temporary eviction if major building repairs, additions, or alterations are necessary that cannot be completed while the lessee lives there.
explanation: Lexical synonym reformulation preserving identical statutory obligation.

original: In the event of the death of the landlord or the tenant, the tenancy shall continue between the legal heirs of the landlord and the tenant, as the case may be, on the same terms and conditions as specified in the tenancy agreement.
simplified: If either the lessor or property owner or tenant passes away, the tenancy continues on identical terms between the surviving heirs of the respective parties.
explanation: Lexical synonym reformulation preserving identical statutory obligation.

original: In 2011, a Bill to amend the 1986 Act was introduced to enable consumers to file online complaints, and against unfair terms in a contract. However, the Bill lapsed with the dissolution of the 15th Lok Sabha. The Consumer Protection Bill, 2015 was introduced in Lok Sabha to replace the 1986 Act. The Bill introduced various new provisions, which included: (i) product liability; (ii) unfair contracts; and (iii) setting up of a regulatory body. The Bill was examined by the Standing Committee on Consumer Affairs which submitted its report in April 2016. The Committee gave several recommendations with regard to: (i) product liability; (ii) powers and functions of the regulatory body (Central Consumer Protection Authority) being set up; (iii) penalties for misleading advertisements and endorsers of such advertisements; and (iv) pecuniary jurisdiction of the adjudicatory body at the district level. The Consumer Protection Bill, 2018 was introduced in January 2018 to replace the 2015 Bill.

original: [CON-HI-004] दुकानदार एमआरपी से अधिक मूल्य पर उत्पाद की बिक्री नहीं करेगा।

original: [CON-HI-083] ई-कॉमर्स मंच पर ग्राहक शिकायत अधिकारी का नाम व ईमेल पता प्रकाशित करना अनिवार्य है।
simplified: [CON-HI-083] ऑनलाइन शॉपिंग साइट्स पर ग्रीवेंस ऑफिसर का संपर्क विवरण देना जरूरी है।
explanation: शिकायत अधिकारी विवरण अनिवार्यता सुरक्षित।

original: [CON-HI-084] दुकानदार एमआरपी से अधिक मूल्य पर उत्पाद की बिक्री नहीं करेगा।
simplified: [CON-HI-084] व्यापारी पैकेट पर छपे अधिकतम खुदरा मूल्य (एमआरपी) से ज्यादा पैसा नहीं ले सकता।
explanation: एमआरपी सीमा का नियम सुरक्षित।

original: [CON-HI-085] दोष सिद्ध होने पर आयोग अनुचित अनुबंध की शर्तों को निरस्त कर सकता है।
simplified: [CON-HI-085] आयोग उपभोक्ताओं के शोषण वाले एकतरफा अनुबंधों को रद्द घोषित कर सकता है।
explanation: अनुचित शर्तें रद्द करने का अधिकार सुरक्षित।

original: A consumer means any person who buys any goods for a consideration which has been paid or promised or partly paid and partly promised, or under any system of deferred payment, but does not include a person who obtains such goods for resale or for any commercial purpose.
simplified: A consumer is anyone who purchases goods or services for personal use with paid or deferred consideration, excluding those who buy for commercial resale or business profit.
explanation: Statutory consumer right preserved (Consumer Protection Act 2019, Section 2(7)).

original: A consumer means any person who buys any goods for a consideration which has been paid or promised or partly paid and partly promised, or under any system of deferred payment, but does not include a person who obtains such goods for resale or for any commercial purpose.
simplified: A consumer is any commercial corporation that buys bulk goods for industrial resale on wholesale markets.
explanation: Exclusion of commercial resale inverted into defining characteristic of consumer.

original: A consumer means any person who buys any goods for a consideration which has been paid or promised or partly paid and partly promised, or under any system of deferred payment, but does not include a person who obtains such goods for resale or for any commercial purpose.
simplified: Anyone who buys goods for personal use is a consumer, and they are completely immune from paying any consideration.
explanation: Requirement of paying consideration erased.

original: A consumer means any person who buys any goods for a consideration which has been paid or promised or partly paid and partly promised, or under any system of deferred payment, but does not include a person who obtains such goods for resale or for any commercial purpose.
simplified: A consumer is anyone who buys goods for consideration.
explanation: Omitted statutory exclusion of commercial purpose and deferred payment options.

original: Misleading advertisement in relation to any product or service means an advertisement which falsely describes such product or service, or gives a false guarantee to, or is likely to mislead the consumers as to the nature, substance, quantity or quality of such product or service.
simplified: A misleading advertisement is any promotion that falsely describes a product or service, gives fake guarantees, or deceives consumers regarding quality, quantity, or nature.
explanation: Statutory consumer right preserved (Consumer Protection Act 2019, Section 2(28)).

original: Misleading advertisement in relation to any product or service means an advertisement which falsely describes such product or service, or gives a false guarantee to, or is likely to mislead the consumers as to the nature, substance, quantity or quality of such product or service.
simplified: Manufacturers are legally authorized to publish completely fake product descriptions and false guarantees in advertisements.
explanation: Misleading advertisement definition flipped into statutory entitlement.

original: Misleading advertisement in relation to any product or service means an advertisement which falsely describes such product or service, or gives a false guarantee to, or is likely to mislead the consumers as to the nature, substance, quantity or quality of such product or service.
simplified: An advertisement is misleading only if it has already caused the physical death of at least five consumers.
explanation: Threshold of deception distorted into extreme physical casualty requirement.

original: Misleading advertisement in relation to any product or service means an advertisement which falsely describes such product or service, or gives a false guarantee to, or is likely to mislead the consumers as to the nature, substance, quantity or quality of such product or service.
simplified: A misleading ad gives false guarantees about product quality.
explanation: Direct plain summary.

original: Product liability means the responsibility of a product manufacturer or product seller, of any product or service, to compensate for any harm caused to a consumer by such defective product manufactured or sold or by deficiency in services relating thereto.
simplified: Product liability is the legal duty of manufacturers and sellers to pay compensation for injury, damage, or loss caused by defective goods or deficient services.
explanation: Statutory consumer right preserved (Consumer Protection Act 2019, Section 2(41)).

original: Product liability means the responsibility of a product manufacturer or product seller, of any product or service, to compensate for any harm caused to a consumer by such defective product manufactured or sold or by deficiency in services relating thereto.
simplified: Consumers must pay financial compensation to manufacturers whenever a factory product breaks down.
explanation: Product liability duty inverted from manufacturer to consumer.

original: Product liability means the responsibility of a product manufacturer or product seller, of any product or service, to compensate for any harm caused to a consumer by such defective product manufactured or sold or by deficiency in services relating thereto.
simplified: Manufacturers may optionally consider apologizing for defective products if they feel like it, with zero financial compensation.
explanation: Strict compensation liability demoted to voluntary courtesy.

original: Product liability means the responsibility of a product manufacturer or product seller, of any product or service, to compensate for any harm caused to a consumer by such defective product manufactured or sold or by deficiency in services relating thereto.
simplified: Product liability requires compensation for harm caused by defective products.
explanation: Accurate plain legal formulation.

original: Unfair contract means a contract between a manufacturer or trader and a consumer, having such terms which cause significant change in the rights of such consumer, including requiring manifestly excessive security deposits, imposing a penalty disproportionate to the loss, or unilateral termination without cause.
simplified: An unfair contract is any consumer agreement containing one-sided terms, such as excessive deposits, disproportionate penalties, or arbitrary landlord/seller cancellation.
explanation: Statutory consumer right preserved (Consumer Protection Act 2019, Section 2(46)).

original: Unfair contract means a contract between a manufacturer or trader and a consumer, having such terms which cause significant change in the rights of such consumer, including requiring manifestly excessive security deposits, imposing a penalty disproportionate to the loss, or unilateral termination without cause.
simplified: Contracts that require infinite deposits and allow sellers to cancel without reason are declared fair and mandatory by law.
explanation: Unfair contract definition inverted into legally encouraged standard.

original: Unfair contract means a contract between a manufacturer or trader and a consumer, having such terms which cause significant change in the rights of such consumer, including requiring manifestly excessive security deposits, imposing a penalty disproportionate to the loss, or unilateral termination without cause.
simplified: An unfair contract contains disproportionate penalties and excessive security deposits.
explanation: Accurate plain summary.

original: Unfair trade practice means a trade practice which, for the purpose of promoting the sale, use or supply of any goods or for the provision of any service, adopts any unfair method or unfair or deceptive practice, including refusing to issue a bill or cash memo.
simplified: An unfair trade practice involves deceptive sales tactics, including misrepresenting product quality or refusing to issue a valid purchase receipt or cash memo.
explanation: Statutory consumer right preserved (Consumer Protection Act 2019, Section 2(47)).

original: Unfair trade practice means a trade practice which, for the purpose of promoting the sale, use or supply of any goods or for the provision of any service, adopts any unfair method or unfair or deceptive practice, including refusing to issue a bill or cash memo.
simplified: Shopkeepers are legally mandated to conceal product defects and strictly prohibited from giving bills or receipts.
explanation: Unfair trade practice prohibited acts converted into mandatory merchant duties.

original: Unfair trade practice means a trade practice which, for the purpose of promoting the sale, use or supply of any goods or for the provision of any service, adopts any unfair method or unfair or deceptive practice, including refusing to issue a bill or cash memo.
simplified: Refusing to issue a cash memo is an unfair trade practice.
explanation: Concise plain reformulation.

original: The Central Government shall, by notification, establish an authority to be known as the Central Consumer Protection Authority to regulate matters relating to violation of rights of consumers, unfair trade practices and false or misleading advertisements which are prejudicial to the interests of public and consumers.
simplified: The government must establish the Central Consumer Protection Authority (CCPA) to enforce consumer rights, crack down on unfair trade practices, and stop misleading ads.
explanation: Statutory consumer right preserved (Consumer Protection Act 2019, Section 10(1)).

original: The Central Government shall, by notification, establish an authority to be known as the Central Consumer Protection Authority to regulate matters relating to violation of rights of consumers, unfair trade practices and false or misleading advertisements which are prejudicial to the interests of public and consumers.
simplified: Private retail associations can dissolve the consumer protection authority at will.
explanation: Statutory regulatory authority dismantled by private trade associations.

original: The Central Government shall, by notification, establish an authority to be known as the Central Consumer Protection Authority to regulate matters relating to violation of rights of consumers, unfair trade practices and false or misleading advertisements which are prejudicial to the interests of public and consumers.
simplified: The Central Consumer Authority regulates consumer rights and false advertisements.
explanation: Faithful plain simplification.

original: Where the Central Authority is satisfied after inquiry that an advertisement is false or misleading and is prejudicial to the interest of any consumer, it may issue directions to the concerned trader, manufacturer, endorser or publisher to discontinue or modify such advertisement within such time as specified.
simplified: If the CCPA finds an ad to be false or deceptive, it can legally order the advertiser, manufacturer, celebrity endorser, or publisher to modify or immediately take down the ad.
explanation: Statutory consumer right preserved (Consumer Protection Act 2019, Section 21(1)).

original: Where the Central Authority is satisfied after inquiry that an advertisement is false or misleading and is prejudicial to the interest of any consumer, it may issue directions to the concerned trader, manufacturer, endorser or publisher to discontinue or modify such advertisement within such time as specified.
simplified: The CCPA is strictly barred from interfering with false ads and must allow celebrities to endorse harmful fake drugs freely.
explanation: Regulatory enforcement power completely negated.

original: Where the Central Authority is satisfied after inquiry that an advertisement is false or misleading and is prejudicial to the interest of any consumer, it may issue directions to the concerned trader, manufacturer, endorser or publisher to discontinue or modify such advertisement within such time as specified.
simplified: The Central Authority may order the removal or modification of misleading advertisements.
explanation: Direct plain statement.

original: The Central Authority may, by order, impose on a manufacturer or endorser a penalty which may extend to ten lakh rupees for a false or misleading advertisement, and for every subsequent contravention, a penalty which may extend to fifty lakh rupees.
simplified: The CCPA can fine manufacturers or celebrity endorsers up to 10 lakh rupees for a misleading ad, and up to 50 lakh rupees for repeat offenses.
explanation: Statutory consumer right preserved (Consumer Protection Act 2019, Section 21(2)).

original: The Central Authority may, by order, impose on a manufacturer or endorser a penalty which may extend to ten lakh rupees for a false or misleading advertisement, and for every subsequent contravention, a penalty which may extend to fifty lakh rupees.
simplified: The CCPA can fine advertisers up to ten rupees for the first offense and fifty rupees thereafter.
explanation: Statutory financial penalties reduced from lakhs to nominal rupees.

original: The Central Authority may, by order, impose on a manufacturer or endorser a penalty which may extend to ten lakh rupees for a false or misleading advertisement, and for every subsequent contravention, a penalty which may extend to fifty lakh rupees.
simplified: Celebrities endorsing fake ads are awarded a cash reward of ten lakh rupees from the government.
explanation: Statutory penalty converted into state reward.

original: The Central Authority may, by order, impose on a manufacturer or endorser a penalty which may extend to ten lakh rupees for a false or misleading advertisement, and for every subsequent contravention, a penalty which may extend to fifty lakh rupees.
simplified: The CCPA can impose fines up to 10 lakh rupees, increasing to 50 lakh for repeat offenses.
explanation: Accurate plain summary.

original: Subject to the other provisions of this Act, the District Commission shall have jurisdiction to entertain complaints where the value of the goods or services paid as consideration does not exceed fifty lakh rupees.
simplified: The District Consumer Commission has legal jurisdiction to resolve consumer disputes where the total value of goods or services does not exceed 50 lakh rupees.
explanation: Statutory consumer right preserved (Consumer Protection Act 2019, Section 34(1)).

original: Subject to the other provisions of this Act, the District Commission shall have jurisdiction to entertain complaints where the value of the goods or services paid as consideration does not exceed fifty lakh rupees.
simplified: The District Commission can only hear complaints where consideration exceeds five hundred crore rupees.
explanation: Jurisdictional ceiling distorted from 50 lakhs to 500 crores.

original: Subject to the other provisions of this Act, the District Commission shall have jurisdiction to entertain complaints where the value of the goods or services paid as consideration does not exceed fifty lakh rupees.
simplified: The District Commission hears consumer complaints under 50 lakh rupees.
explanation: Direct plain reformulation.

original: A complaint, in relation to any goods sold or delivered or agreed to be sold or delivered or any service provided or agreed to be provided, may be filed with a District Commission by the consumer, or any recognized consumer association, or the Central Authority.
simplified: A consumer complaint can be filed with the District Commission by an individual consumer, a recognized consumer association, or the Central Authority.
explanation: Statutory consumer right preserved (Consumer Protection Act 2019, Section 35(1)).

original: A complaint, in relation to any goods sold or delivered or agreed to be sold or delivered or any service provided or agreed to be provided, may be filed with a District Commission by the consumer, or any recognized consumer association, or the Central Authority.
simplified: Only the offending company has the right to file cases, and individual consumers are strictly barred from entering the court.
explanation: Standing inverted to exclude consumers.

original: A complaint, in relation to any goods sold or delivered or agreed to be sold or delivered or any service provided or agreed to be provided, may be filed with a District Commission by the consumer, or any recognized consumer association, or the Central Authority.
simplified: Consumers, consumer associations, or the CCPA can file complaints with the District Commission.
explanation: Accurate plain reformulation.

original: Subject to the other provisions of this Act, the State Commission shall have jurisdiction to entertain complaints where the value of the goods or services paid as consideration exceeds fifty lakh rupees, but does not exceed two crore rupees.
simplified: The State Consumer Commission handles complaints where the value of goods or services is between 50 lakh rupees and 2 crore rupees.
explanation: Statutory consumer right preserved (Consumer Protection Act 2019, Section 47(1)).

original: Subject to the other provisions of this Act, the State Commission shall have jurisdiction to entertain complaints where the value of the goods or services paid as consideration exceeds fifty lakh rupees, but does not exceed two crore rupees.
simplified: The State Commission handles complaints between fifty rupees and two hundred rupees.
explanation: Pecuniary jurisdiction distorted from crores to rupees.

original: Subject to the other provisions of this Act, the State Commission shall have jurisdiction to entertain complaints where the value of the goods or services paid as consideration exceeds fifty lakh rupees, but does not exceed two crore rupees.
simplified: The State Commission hears complaints between 50 lakhs and 2 crores.
explanation: Accurate plain summary.

original: Subject to the other provisions of this Act, the National Commission shall have jurisdiction to entertain complaints where the value of the goods or services paid as consideration exceeds two crore rupees.
simplified: The National Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission (NCDRC) hears major consumer complaints where the value of goods or services exceeds 2 crore rupees.
explanation: Statutory consumer right preserved (Consumer Protection Act 2019, Section 58(1)).

original: Subject to the other provisions of this Act, the National Commission shall have jurisdiction to entertain complaints where the value of the goods or services paid as consideration exceeds two crore rupees.
simplified: The National Commission is restricted to hearing petty claims under ten rupees only.
explanation: Jurisdiction ceiling drastically inverted.

original: Subject to the other provisions of this Act, the National Commission shall have jurisdiction to entertain complaints where the value of the goods or services paid as consideration exceeds two crore rupees.
simplified: The National Commission handles consumer complaints exceeding 2 crore rupees.
explanation: Plain legal summary.

original: The District Commission, the State Commission or the National Commission shall not admit a complaint unless it is filed within two years from the date on which the cause of action has arisen.
simplified: Consumer complaints must be filed within two years from the date the dispute or defect occurred, or they will be barred by limitation.
explanation: Statutory consumer right preserved (Consumer Protection Act 2019, Section 69(1)).

original: The District Commission, the State Commission or the National Commission shall not admit a complaint unless it is filed within two years from the date on which the cause of action has arisen.
simplified: A consumer complaint can only be filed within 24 hours of buying the product.
explanation: Statutory limitation period slashed from 2 years to 24 hours.

original: The District Commission, the State Commission or the National Commission shall not admit a complaint unless it is filed within two years from the date on which the cause of action has arisen.
simplified: Consumer complaints must be filed within two years of the cause of action.
explanation: Accurate plain reformulation.

original: A product manufacturer shall be liable in a product liability action, if the product contains a manufacturing defect, or is defective in design, or there is a deviation from manufacturing specifications, or the product does not conform to the express warranty.
simplified: A manufacturer is legally liable for damages if their product has a manufacturing defect, unsafe design, deviates from technical specifications, or breaches an express warranty.
explanation: Statutory consumer right preserved (Consumer Protection Act 2019, Section 84).

original: A product manufacturer shall be liable in a product liability action, if the product contains a manufacturing defect, or is defective in design, or there is a deviation from manufacturing specifications, or the product does not conform to the express warranty.
simplified: Manufacturers have zero liability for fatal product design flaws and all victims must pay the company for product wear.
explanation: Product liability erased and shifted to consumer punishment.

original: A product manufacturer shall be liable in a product liability action, if the product contains a manufacturing defect, or is defective in design, or there is a deviation from manufacturing specifications, or the product does not conform to the express warranty.
simplified: Manufacturers are liable for design flaws, manufacturing defects, or warranty breaches.
explanation: Direct plain statement.

original: A product manufacturer shall not be liable in a product liability action where the product was misused, altered, or modified at the time the harm was caused.
simplified: A manufacturer is exempt from product liability if the consumer misused, unauthorizedly modified, or tampered with the product when the injury occurred.
explanation: Statutory consumer right preserved (Consumer Protection Act 2019, Section 87).

original: A product manufacturer shall not be liable in a product liability action where the product was misused, altered, or modified at the time the harm was caused.
simplified: A manufacturer remains strictly liable even if the consumer deliberately dropped the television from an airplane and modified it with explosives.
explanation: Statutory defense of consumer misuse/alteration completely deleted.

original: A product manufacturer shall not be liable in a product liability action where the product was misused, altered, or modified at the time the harm was caused.
simplified: Manufacturers are not liable if the product was misused or modified by the user.
explanation: Accurate plain reformulation.

original: Every e-commerce entity shall display prominently to its users the legal name of the entity, principal geographic address of its headquarters and all branches, name and details of its website, and contact details including email, customer care number of grievance officer.
simplified: Online shopping platforms must clearly display their registered business name, official address, customer care details, and the name and email of their Grievance Officer.
explanation: Statutory consumer right preserved (Consumer Protection (E-Commerce) Rules 2020, Rule 5).

original: Every e-commerce entity shall display prominently to its users the legal name of the entity, principal geographic address of its headquarters and all branches, name and details of its website, and contact details including email, customer care number of grievance officer.
simplified: E-commerce platforms are required by law to remain completely anonymous and never reveal any physical address or customer support contact.
explanation: Transparency duty inverted into mandatory secrecy.

original: Every e-commerce entity shall display prominently to its users the legal name of the entity, principal geographic address of its headquarters and all branches, name and details of its website, and contact details including email, customer care number of grievance officer.
simplified: Online platforms must display company contact and grievance officer details.
explanation: Plain language summary.

original: Every marketplace e-commerce entity shall ensure that the country of origin of the goods is clearly displayed to enable the consumer to make an informed decision at the pre-purchase stage.
simplified: Online marketplaces must clearly display the country of origin on all product listings before a consumer makes a purchase.
explanation: Statutory consumer right preserved (Consumer Protection (E-Commerce) Rules 2020, Rule 6).

original: Every marketplace e-commerce entity shall ensure that the country of origin of the goods is clearly displayed to enable the consumer to make an informed decision at the pre-purchase stage.
simplified: Online sellers are strictly forbidden from showing where a product was made, and must conceal the country of origin.
explanation: Country of origin disclosure reversed to mandatory concealment.

original: Every marketplace e-commerce entity shall ensure that the country of origin of the goods is clearly displayed to enable the consumer to make an informed decision at the pre-purchase stage.
simplified: Marketplace platforms must display the country of origin for all goods.
explanation: Accurate plain legal reformulation.

original: Any person aggrieved by an order made by the District Commission may prefer an appeal against such order to the State Commission within a period of forty-five days from the date of the order.
simplified: Anyone dissatisfied with a District Commission order can appeal to the State Consumer Commission within 45 days.
explanation: Statutory consumer right preserved (Consumer Protection Act 2019, Section 41).

original: Any person aggrieved by an order made by the District Commission may prefer an appeal against such order to the State Commission within a period of forty-five days from the date of the order.
simplified: Appeals against District Commission orders must be filed within 24 hours or right of appeal is forfeited.
explanation: Appeal period slashed from 45 days to 24 hours.

original: Any person aggrieved by an order made by the District Commission may prefer an appeal against such order to the State Commission within a period of forty-five days from the date of the order.
simplified: Orders of the District Commission are completely final and cannot be appealed to any higher commission.
explanation: Right of appeal extinguished.

original: Any person aggrieved by an order made by the District Commission may prefer an appeal against such order to the State Commission within a period of forty-five days from the date of the order.
simplified: Appeals to the State Commission must be filed within 45 days.
explanation: Direct plain statement.

original: The State Government shall establish a consumer mediation cell to be attached to each of the District Commissions and the State Commission of that State.
simplified: State governments must set up consumer mediation cells attached to every District and State Consumer Commission to resolve disputes through settlement.
explanation: Statutory consumer right preserved (Consumer Protection Act 2019, Section 74).

original: The State Government shall establish a consumer mediation cell to be attached to each of the District Commissions and the State Commission of that State.
simplified: Mediation cells are strictly prohibited in consumer forums and all settlements out of court are illegal.
explanation: Mediation mandate inverted to statutory ban.

original: The State Government shall establish a consumer mediation cell to be attached to each of the District Commissions and the State Commission of that State.
simplified: State governments must establish consumer mediation cells attached to consumer commissions.
explanation: Accurate plain reformulation.

original: Any manufacturer or service provider who causes a false or misleading advertisement to be made which is prejudicial to the interest of consumers shall be punished with imprisonment for a term which may extend to two years and with fine which may extend to ten lakh rupees.
simplified: Publishing false or misleading ads that harm consumers is a criminal offense punishable by up to two years in prison and a fine of up to 10 lakh rupees.
explanation: Statutory consumer right preserved (Consumer Protection Act 2019, Section 89).

original: Any manufacturer or service provider who causes a false or misleading advertisement to be made which is prejudicial to the interest of consumers shall be punished with imprisonment for a term which may extend to two years and with fine which may extend to ten lakh rupees.
simplified: False advertising is awarded a government tax rebate and immune from all criminal penalties.
explanation: Criminal penal sanction inverted to state subsidy.

original: Any manufacturer or service provider who causes a false or misleading advertisement to be made which is prejudicial to the interest of consumers shall be punished with imprisonment for a term which may extend to two years and with fine which may extend to ten lakh rupees.
simplified: Misleading advertising can be punished with up to 2 years prison and 10 lakh fine.
explanation: Accurate plain summary.

original: उपभोक्ता से ऐसा कोई व्यक्ति अभिप्रेत है जो किसी ऐसे प्रतिफल के बदले कोई माल खरीदता है जिसका संदाय कर दिया गया है या संदाय करने का वचन दिया गया है, किन्तु इसके अंतर्गत ऐसा व्यक्ति नहीं आता जो ऐसे माल को पुनर्विक्रय या किसी वाणिज्यिक प्रयोजन के लिए अभिप्राप्त करता है।
simplified: उपभोक्ता वह व्यक्ति है जो अपने निजी उपयोग के लिए तय कीमत चुकाकर माल या सेवा खरीदता है, जिसमें व्यापारिक मुनाफे या दोबारा बेचने के लिए खरीदने वाले शामिल नहीं हैं।
explanation: उपभोक्ता संरक्षण विधिक प्रावधान (उपभोक्ता संरक्षण अधिनियम 2019, धारा 2(7))।

original: उपभोक्ता से ऐसा कोई व्यक्ति अभिप्रेत है जो किसी ऐसे प्रतिफल के बदले कोई माल खरीदता है जिसका संदाय कर दिया गया है या संदाय करने का वचन दिया गया है, किन्तु इसके अंतर्गत ऐसा व्यक्ति नहीं आता जो ऐसे माल को पुनर्विक्रय या किसी वाणिज्यिक प्रयोजन के लिए अभिप्राप्त करता है।
simplified: व्यापारिक मुनाफे के लिए थोक में सामान खरीदने वाली बड़ी कंपनियां ही कानूनन एकमात्र असली उपभोक्ता मानी जाएंगी।
explanation: वाणिज्यिक अपवर्जन का सीधा खंडन।

original: उपभोक्ता से ऐसा कोई व्यक्ति अभिप्रेत है जो किसी ऐसे प्रतिफल के बदले कोई माल खरीदता है जिसका संदाय कर दिया गया है या संदाय करने का वचन दिया गया है, किन्तु इसके अंतर्गत ऐसा व्यक्ति नहीं आता जो ऐसे माल को पुनर्विक्रय या किसी वाणिज्यिक प्रयोजन के लिए अभिप्राप्त करता है।
simplified: उपभोक्ता वह है जो अपने उपयोग के लिए भुगतान करके सामान खरीदता है।
explanation: सटीक विधिक रूप।

original: भ्रामक विज्ञापन से ऐसा विज्ञापन अभिप्रेत है जो किसी उत्पाद या सेवा का मिथ्या वर्णन करता है या मिथ्या गारंटी देता है या जो उपभोक्ताओं को प्रकृति, सार, मात्रा या गुणवत्ता के बारे में गुमराह करता है।
